# DAIV

> DAIV is an open-source, self-hosted SWE agent for GitLab and GitHub that turns issues into merge requests, answers review comments, and fixes failing CI.

DAIV is an open-source async software engineering agent that integrates natively with GitLab and GitHub through webhooks. Create an issue, get a merge request. Mention DAIV in a review, get the fix. Licensed under Apache 2.0.


# Getting Started

# Quickstart

This page gets you from a clean machine to a first merge request in about 15 minutes: you run DAIV on one Linux host with Docker Compose, connect a GitLab project, and let DAIV turn an issue into a merge request.

It is a trial setup: one worker, no email, no single sign-on. For a production install, or to connect GitHub, follow [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md) and [Platform setup](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/platform-setup/index.md).

## Before you start

You need:

- **A Linux host with Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2.** About 3 GB of free disk: the DAIV images are about 1.1 GB, and the image the sandbox runs the agent in is another 1.1 GB, pulled on the first run.
- **An [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys).** To use another provider, see [LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md).
- **A GitLab project** on GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab, where you are a Maintainer or Owner.
- **A URL GitLab can reach DAIV at.** GitLab tells DAIV about new issues and comments with webhooks, so it must be able to open DAIV's port 8000:
  - **Self-managed GitLab on your network:** the host's address, such as `http://192.168.1.10:8000`, is enough once an admin allows requests to the local network under **Admin** → **Settings** → **Network** → **Outbound requests**. Without that, GitLab refuses the webhook with `Url is blocked: Requests to the local network are not allowed`.
  - **GitLab.com:** a public URL, such as a server with a domain behind a reverse proxy, or an HTTPS tunnel to port 8000 on your machine.

## Create a GitLab account for DAIV

DAIV works as a GitLab user: it comments, pushes and opens merge requests as that user, and it ignores comments written by that user. Give DAIV its own account; if it uses your token, it ignores your comments, including the one that approves its plan.

Can't create a second account?

Use a token from your own account, and label issues `daiv-auto` instead of `daiv` in [Get your first merge request](#get-your-first-merge-request): DAIV then plans and implements without waiting for an approval comment. You won't be able to talk to DAIV in comments.

1. Create a user for DAIV, for example `daiv`. On GitLab.com, sign up a second account; on a self-managed GitLab, an admin creates it under **Admin** → **Users** → **New user**.
1. In your project, add that user with the **Maintainer** role under **Manage** → **Members** → **Invite members**. DAIV only sets up webhooks on projects where its user is a Maintainer or Owner.
1. Sign in to GitLab as that user.
1. Select your avatar → **Edit profile** → **Access tokens**, and create a personal access token with the `api` scope.
1. Copy the token. GitLab shows it once.

## Create the configuration

Create a directory for DAIV, and in it a certificate authority for the sandbox's egress proxy. DAIV runs git inside the [sandbox](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/index.md); the proxy is what lets those commands reach GitLab, adding the credentials so the token never enters the sandbox.

```
mkdir daiv && cd daiv
mkdir certs
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 3650 -subj "/CN=daiv-sandbox-egress" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" \
  -keyout certs/egress-ca.key -out certs/egress-ca.crt
```

The sandbox service runs as UID 1001, so it needs read access to the key. Make the key readable:

```
chmod 644 certs/egress-ca.key
```

Create the `.env` file. The command fills in the random secrets and the Docker socket's group for you:

```
cat > .env <<EOF
DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL=http://192.168.1.10:8000
CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.com
CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN=<gitlab-token>
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<openrouter-api-key>
DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
DB_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
DOCKER_GID=$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)
EOF
chmod 600 .env
```

Then replace the first four values. `<gitlab-token>` and `<openrouter-api-key>` are placeholders for the values of `CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`:

| Variable                     | Set it to                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`          | The URL GitLab can reach DAIV at, without a trailing slash (see [Before you start](#before-you-start))                                                                    |
| `CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL`        | Your GitLab's URL, as DAIV's containers reach it                                                                                                                          |
| `CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN` | The token of DAIV's GitLab user, from [Create a GitLab account for DAIV](#create-a-gitlab-account-for-daiv)                                                               |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`         | Your OpenRouter API key. DAIV reads it once, on the first start; see [Provider API keys](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/#provider-api-keys) |

Create `docker-compose.yml` next to it:

```
x-daiv: &daiv
  image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main}
  restart: unless-stopped
  env_file: .env
  environment:
    DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: daiv.settings.production
    DJANGO_REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
    DB_HOST: db
    DB_NAME: daiv
    DB_USER: daiv
    DB_SSLMODE: prefer
    CODEBASE_CLIENT: gitlab
    EMAIL_BACKEND: django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend # (1)!
  volumes:
    - media:/home/daiv/data/media
  ulimits:
    nofile:
      soft: 65536
      hard: 524288

x-background: &background
  <<: *daiv
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q -e db_worker -e crontask /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null"]
    interval: 30s
  depends_on:
    app:
      condition: service_healthy

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17.6
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: daiv
      POSTGRES_USER: daiv
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U daiv -d daiv"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:8.6-alpine # (2)!
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - redis:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 5

  app:
    <<: *daiv
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  worker:
    <<: *background
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-worker # (3)!

  scheduler:
    <<: *background
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-crontask # (4)!

  sandbox:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv-sandbox:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    group_add:
      - ${DOCKER_GID}
    environment:
      DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY: ${DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY}
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_CERT_FILE: /home/app/certs/egress-ca.crt
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_KEY_FILE: /home/app/certs/egress-ca.key
      DAIV_SANDBOX_REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/3
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock # (5)!
      - ./certs:/home/app/certs:ro

volumes:
  db:
  redis:
  media:
```

1. Prints sign-in emails to the app's log instead of sending them, so you need no mail server. [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md) shows how to configure SMTP.
1. DAIV needs Redis 8 or later: the agent's checkpoints use its search commands, which Redis 7 does not have.
1. One worker that serves every queue. [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md) splits agent runs and short interactive tasks across two.
1. Runs DAIV's periodic tasks, among them adding the webhook to your GitLab projects.
1. The sandbox starts a container for each agent run through the Docker socket.

## Start DAIV

Start the stack from the directory that holds `docker-compose.yml`:

```
docker compose up -d --wait
```

The first start pulls about 1.2 GB of images and runs the database migrations; the command returns once every service is healthy, usually within three minutes. If it reports an unhealthy service, `docker compose logs app` shows why.

## Sign in

Signing in is optional for the first merge request, but the dashboard is where you watch DAIV work.

Sign in over HTTPS or on localhost

DAIV's session cookie, which also carries the CSRF token, is a secure cookie, so a browser keeps it only on `https://` URLs and on `localhost`. Over plain `http://` to any other address, sign-in fails with **CSRF verification failed**. If DAIV runs on another machine, forward the port with `ssh -L 8000:localhost:8000 <host>` and open `http://localhost:8000`, or put DAIV behind HTTPS.

1. Create the first admin with [`bootstrap_admin`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#bootstrap_admin), replacing `you@example.com` with your email address:

   ```
   docker compose exec app django-admin bootstrap_admin you@example.com
   ```

1. On the DAIV host, open `http://localhost:8000/accounts/login/`.

1. Enter that email address.

1. Select **Continue with email**.

1. Read the one-time code from the log:

   ```
   docker compose logs app | grep -A2 "sign-in code"
   ```

1. Enter the code.

1. Select **Verify & sign in**.

## Connect your GitLab project

DAIV adds a webhook to every project its user maintains within five minutes. To add it now:

1. Run [`setup_webhooks`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#setup_webhooks):

   ```
   docker compose exec app django-admin setup_webhooks
   ```

1. In your project, open **Settings** → **Webhooks**. It lists `<DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL>/api/codebase/callbacks/gitlab/`, with `<DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL>` replaced by your `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` value.

1. Select **Test** → **Push events**. GitLab shows HTTP 204.

## Get your first merge request

1. In the project, create an issue, for example *Add a `hello_world()` function that returns "Hello, world!"*.
1. Add the `daiv` label to the issue. If the project has no `daiv` label yet, create it from the label picker.
1. Wait for the plan. DAIV reacts to the issue with the eyes emoji (👀) within seconds, and posts an implementation plan as a comment, usually within a minute.
1. Approve the plan with a comment that mentions DAIV's user, for example `@daiv proceed`.
1. Wait for the merge request. DAIV implements the plan and opens a merge request, usually within a few minutes. The first run takes longer while the sandbox pulls its image.

See [Issue addressing](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/issue-addressing/index.md) for what else you can do on an issue.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                       | Likely cause                                                         | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing happens after you add the label       | The webhook is missing, or GitLab can't reach `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`    | Run `setup_webhooks` as in [Connect your GitLab project](#connect-your-gitlab-project) and check that DAIV's user is a Maintainer. Under **Settings** → **Webhooks** → **Edit** → **Recent events**, GitLab shows each delivery and its error |
| DAIV ignores your comment                     | You commented as DAIV's own user, or didn't mention its username     | Comment from your own account and mention DAIV's user                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| DAIV comments *An unexpected error occurred*  | The run failed                                                       | `docker compose logs worker sandbox` shows the error                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Sign-in fails with *Server Error (500)*       | DAIV couldn't send the sign-in email                                 | Keep `EMAIL_BACKEND` as above, or configure SMTP as in [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md)                                                                                                       |
| Sign-in fails with *CSRF verification failed* | You opened DAIV over plain HTTP on an address other than `localhost` | See [Sign in](#sign-in)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Remove DAIV

Remove DAIV and everything it stored when you are done with the trial.

This deletes the database

`docker compose down -v` removes the volumes, including the database volume `db`: every user, session and setting is lost, and you cannot restore them.

1. From the directory that holds `docker-compose.yml`, remove the containers and volumes:

   ```
   docker compose down -v
   ```

1. Remove the containers the sandbox started:

   ```
   docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq --filter label=daiv.sandbox.type)
   ```

## Next steps

- **[Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md)** — a production install: Docker Swarm, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, email and single sign-on
- **[Repository configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/index.md)** — tune DAIV per repository with `.daiv.yml`
- **[Pull request assistant](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/pull-request-assistant/index.md)** — mention DAIV on a merge request to get a review or a fix

# Deployment

This page deploys a self-hosted DAIV with Docker Swarm or Docker Compose, puts it behind an Nginx reverse proxy, and creates the first admin. Afterwards you have a DAIV instance ready to connect to your codebase.

To try DAIV on one machine first, follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/quickstart/index.md).

## Requirements

| Requirement    | Version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker Engine  | The samples pin no minimum. Docker Swarm needs Swarm mode enabled on the host.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Docker Compose | 2.17.0 or later, which provides the `docker compose` command and `depends_on.restart`. Only the Compose deployment needs it.                                                                                                                          |
| PostgreSQL     | 15 or later, the minimum of the Django release DAIV pins; the samples run `postgres:17.6`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Redis          | 8 or later. The samples run `redis:8.6-alpine`. The agent's checkpoints use Redis search commands that Redis 7 lacks, and they must stay on database `0`; see [Redis](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#redis).                 |
| daiv-sandbox   | The samples pull `ghcr.io/srtab/daiv-sandbox:latest`. Update the sandbox together with DAIV: multi-repository sessions need a release with `repos_archive` support and path-scoped egress rules, and DAIV reports an error when the sandbox lacks it. |

You also need a domain name that points to your server, with an SSL certificate for it, and a way for your Git platform to reach `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`. Your Git platform sends webhooks to that URL.

## Services DAIV runs

DAIV needs these services. The samples below run all of them:

- **[PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/)** stores application data.
- **[Redis](https://redis.io/)** holds the cache, sessions and the agent's checkpoints.
- **[DAIV app](https://github.com/srtab/daiv)** (`app`) serves the web dashboard and the API.
- **[DAIV worker](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/topics/tasks/)** (`worker` and `worker-interactive`) runs background tasks.
- **[DAIV scheduler](https://pypi.org/project/django-crontask/)** (`scheduler`) runs periodic tasks, among them adding webhooks to your GitLab projects and syncing repository access.
- **[DAIV sandbox](https://github.com/srtab/daiv-sandbox)** (`sandbox`) runs the agent's commands and git in isolated containers, through an egress proxy that holds the git credentials. See [Sandbox](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/index.md).

Task queues

Background work is split in two: `default` carries agent runs, which hold a worker for as long as the run lasts, while `interactive` carries short user-visible work: session titles, run classification and notification delivery. The `worker` and `worker-interactive` services each serve one of them, so a title never queues behind a run. A worker started with no queue argument serves every queue, which suits a small deployment that accepts that wait.

## Deploy with Docker Swarm

Docker Swarm gives you service discovery, load balancing and rolling updates, so it suits production. These steps deploy to a single server; to extend the stack to more servers, see the [Docker Swarm documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/swarm-tutorial/).

Before you start, [install Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) and [enable Swarm](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/swarm-tutorial/), and check the [requirements](#requirements).

1. Create the first seven Docker secrets listed in [Swarm secrets](#swarm-secrets), with this command (see [Docker secret create](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/secret/create/)), replacing `<name>` and `<value>`:

   ```
   printf '%s' '<value>' | docker secret create <name> -
   ```

1. Create the egress CA. The sandbox reaches your Git platform only through a per-session proxy that adds the credentials, so the token never enters the sandbox, and the proxy signs with this CA:

   ```
   openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 3650 -subj "/CN=daiv-sandbox-egress" \
     -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" \
     -keyout egress-ca.key -out egress-ca.crt
   ```

1. Store the CA as the two secrets the stack reads:

   ```
   docker secret create daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert egress-ca.crt
   docker secret create daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key egress-ca.key
   ```

1. On each node, add this to `/etc/docker/daemon.json`. Each agent run holds many concurrent sockets (sandbox, LLM API, tracing, database, Redis, git over HTTPS), and Docker's default soft limit of 1024 open files fails under load with `[Errno 24] Too many open files`. Swarm ignores service-level `ulimits`, so the daemon must raise `nofile`:

   ```
   {
     "default-ulimits": {
       "nofile": { "Name": "nofile", "Soft": 65536, "Hard": 524288 }
     }
   }
   ```

1. On each node, restart Docker:

   ```
   systemctl restart docker
   ```

1. Save the [Swarm stack file](#swarm-stack-file) as `stack.yml`, and replace each annotated value with your own. [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/index.md) lists the options.

1. From the directory that holds `stack.yml`, deploy the stack:

   ```
   docker stack deploy -c stack.yml daiv
   ```

1. Wait until every service is healthy, which takes several minutes while Docker pulls the images and DAIV migrates the database:

   ```
   docker stack ps daiv --no-trunc
   ```

1. [Put DAIV behind Nginx](#put-daiv-behind-nginx), so you can reach it over HTTPS.

1. Create the first admin by running [`bootstrap_admin`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#bootstrap_admin) in the app's container, replacing `admin@example.com` with the admin's email address:

   ```
   docker exec -it $(docker ps -q -f name=daiv_app | head -n 1) django-admin bootstrap_admin admin@example.com
   ```

1. Open `/accounts/login/` and sign in with the one-time code DAIV emails to that address.

If you turn on OAuth login before anyone signs in, the first Git platform sign-in becomes the admin instead. [The first admin](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#the-first-admin) explains both paths, and [Accounts and roles](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/index.md) covers adding users.

### Swarm secrets

The stack reads these Docker secrets. Create the first seven rows in step 1, and the next two in steps 2 and 3. The last two are optional.

| Secret                           | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `django_secret_key`              | A random secret key for Django, such as the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`. Keep it backed up: see [Django](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#django).            |
| `db_password`                    | A random password for the PostgreSQL database.                                                                                                                                            |
| `codebase_gitlab_auth_token`     | A GitLab personal access token with the `api` scope. See [Platform setup](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/platform-setup/#gitlab-token-role-and-webhooks).                 |
| `codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret` | A random secret that GitLab sends with each webhook, for DAIV to validate.                                                                                                                |
| `daiv_sandbox_api_key`           | A random API key for the sandbox service.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `email_host_password`            | The SMTP password. DAIV authenticates only when `EMAIL_HOST_USER` is also set. The stack requires the secret to exist, so create it with any value if your relay needs no authentication. |
| `openrouter_api_key`             | An [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys).                                                                                                                             |
| `daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert`    | The egress CA certificate.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key`     | The egress CA private key.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `allauth_client_id`              | **Optional.** The OAuth client ID of your Git platform. See [Authentication](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#authentication).                                     |
| `allauth_client_secret`          | **Optional.** The OAuth client secret of your Git platform.                                                                                                                               |

A secret locks the matching field in the dashboard: DAIV reads the value from the secret and you cannot edit it under **Configuration** → **Authentication**. When you will [turn on OAuth login](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#turn-on-oauth-login) in the dashboard instead, leave `allauth_client_id` and `allauth_client_secret` out of the `app` service's `secrets:` list and out of the top-level `secrets:`, as the stack file below does. To use them, create both secrets, then uncomment those lines.

For another provider's key, create a secret named after its variable in lowercase (`openai_api_key`, `anthropic_api_key` or `google_api_key`) add it to the `secrets:` list of the `app` service, which runs the migration that reads it, and declare it under the top-level `secrets:` with `external: true`. DAIV reads each provider key once, at its first start; see [Provider API keys](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/#provider-api-keys). For further variables you want as secrets, see [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/index.md).

### Swarm stack file

```
x-app-environment-defaults: &app_environment_defaults
  # DJANGO
  DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: daiv.settings.production
  DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS: daiv.example.com,app,127.0.0.1 # (1)!
  DJANGO_REDIS_URL: redis://daiv_redis:6379/0
  DJANGO_REDIS_SESSION_URL: redis://daiv_redis:6379/1
  DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL: https://daiv.example.com # (2)!
  # DATABASE
  DB_NAME: daiv
  DB_USER: daiv_admin
  DB_HOST: daiv_db
  DB_SSLMODE: prefer
  # CODEBASE
  CODEBASE_CLIENT: gitlab
  CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL: https://gitlab.com # (3)!
  # EMAIL
  EMAIL_HOST: smtp.example.com
  EMAIL_PORT: 587
  EMAIL_USE_TLS: true
  EMAIL_HOST_USER: smtp-user # (13)!
  # SANDBOX
  DAIV_SANDBOX_URL: http://sandbox:8000 # (4)!

x-deploy-defaults: &deploy_defaults
  replicas: 1
  update_config:
    order: start-first
    delay: 60s
    failure_action: rollback
  rollback_config:
    parallelism: 0
  restart_policy:
    condition: any
    window: 120s

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17.6
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=daiv
      - POSTGRES_USER=daiv_admin
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password
    networks:
      - internal
    secrets:
      - db_password
    volumes:
      - db-volume:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    healthcheck:
      test: pg_isready -q -d $$POSTGRES_DB -U $$POSTGRES_USER
      interval: 10s
      start_period: 120s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      update_config:
        failure_action: rollback
        delay: 10s
      rollback_config:
        parallelism: 0
      restart_policy:
        condition: any
        window: 120s

  redis:
    image: redis:8.6-alpine # (11)!
    networks:
      - internal
    volumes:
      - redis-volume:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: redis-cli ping || exit 1
      interval: 10s
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults

  app:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main} # (5)!
    environment:
      <<: *app_environment_defaults
    secrets:
      - django_secret_key
      - db_password
      - codebase_gitlab_auth_token
      - codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret
      - daiv_sandbox_api_key
      - openrouter_api_key
      - email_host_password
      # - allauth_client_id  (14)
      # - allauth_client_secret  (14)
    networks:
      - internal
      - external
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media # (10)!
      # - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills  (9)
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults

  worker:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main} # (5)!
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-worker default
    environment:
      <<: *app_environment_defaults
    secrets:
      - django_secret_key
      - db_password
      - codebase_gitlab_auth_token
      - codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret
      - daiv_sandbox_api_key
      - openrouter_api_key
      - email_host_password
    networks:
      - internal
    volumes:
      - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media # (10)!
      # - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro  (9)
    healthcheck:
      test: grep -q 'db_worker' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults
      replicas: 1 # (8)!

  worker-interactive:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main} # (5)!
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-worker interactive
    environment:
      <<: *app_environment_defaults
    secrets:
      - django_secret_key
      - db_password
      - codebase_gitlab_auth_token
      - codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret
      - daiv_sandbox_api_key
      - openrouter_api_key
      - email_host_password
    networks:
      - internal
    volumes:
      - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media # (10)!
      # - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro  (9)
    healthcheck:
      test: grep -q 'db_worker' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults
      replicas: 1

  scheduler:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main} # (5)!
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-crontask
    environment:
      <<: *app_environment_defaults
    secrets:
      - django_secret_key
      - db_password
      - codebase_gitlab_auth_token
      - codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret
      - daiv_sandbox_api_key
      - openrouter_api_key
    networks:
      - internal
    healthcheck:
      test: grep -q 'crontask' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults

  sandbox:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv-sandbox:latest # (5)!
    environment:
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_CERT_FILE: /run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert # (12)!
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key
      DAIV_SANDBOX_REDIS_URL: redis://daiv_redis:6379/3
    networks:
      - internal
    secrets:
      - daiv_sandbox_api_key
      - daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert
      - daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock # (6)!
      - $HOME/.docker/config.json:/home/app/.docker/config.json # (7)!
    deploy:
      <<: *deploy_defaults

networks:
  internal:
    driver: overlay
  external:
    driver: overlay

volumes:
  db-volume:
    driver: local
  redis-volume:
    driver: local
  media-volume:
    driver: local

secrets:
  django_secret_key:
    external: true
  db_password:
    external: true
  codebase_gitlab_auth_token:
    external: true
  codebase_gitlab_webhook_secret:
    external: true
  daiv_sandbox_api_key:
    external: true
  openrouter_api_key:
    external: true
  email_host_password:
    external: true
  daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert:
    external: true
  daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key:
    external: true
  # allauth_client_id:  (14)
  #   external: true
  # allauth_client_secret:  (14)
  #   external: true
```

1. Replace `daiv.example.com` with your domain name, without the scheme (`daiv.example.com`, not `https://daiv.example.com`). Keep `app` and `127.0.0.1` for communication between services.
1. Replace with your full URL, including the scheme (for example `https://daiv.example.com`). Your GitLab sends webhooks to this URL, so it must be able to reach it.
1. Set to your GitLab instance URL (for example `https://gitlab.com` for GitLab.com).
1. Points to the sandbox service. Use `http://sandbox:8000` when the sandbox runs in the same stack.
1. Continuous deploys track the `main` tag. Keep the `${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main}` form on every service, so the Deploy workflow can roll back to a pinned per-commit tag (for example `DAIV_IMAGE_TAG=sha-XXXXXXX`).
1. **Required**: the sandbox needs Docker socket access to create isolated containers.
1. **Optional**: remove this volume if you don't need private registry access.
1. **Scaling**: increase `replicas` to handle more concurrent agent runs (for example `replicas: 3`). A worker runs one task to completion before it claims the next, so concurrency is the number of worker containers. Each claims independently from the queues named in its command.
1. **Optional**: uncomment all three lines to mount [custom global skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/#custom-global-skills) that are available across all repositories. `app` receives uploads from the dashboard, so it mounts the directory read-write; `worker` and `worker-interactive` run the agent, so they can mount it read-only.
1. **Required**: the web and worker containers must share this directory. It holds the [artifacts](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/#artifacts) (reports and other files) the agent publishes: `app` writes them for chat turns and serves them, and `worker` writes them for jobs and webhook runs. Any shared filesystem works; on a multi-node swarm, use a network-backed volume driver.
1. Redis 8 or later; see [Requirements](#requirements).
1. **Required**: the egress CA you stored as secrets in step 3 of [Deploy with Docker Swarm](#deploy-with-docker-swarm). The sandbox's egress proxy signs with it; without it, every agent run fails when the sandbox rejects the session.
1. The SMTP user. DAIV sends the `email_host_password` secret only when this is set; delete the line if your relay needs no authentication. Without an SMTP server, replace the `EMAIL_*` lines with `EMAIL_BACKEND: django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend` and read the sign-in code from `docker service logs daiv_app`.
1. **Optional**: uncomment the two `allauth_*` lines under `app`'s `secrets:` and the two under the top-level `secrets:` only after you create both secrets. DAIV then takes the OAuth client ID and secret from them and locks the fields under **Configuration** → **Authentication**. Leave them commented to set up OAuth login in the dashboard.

## Deploy with Docker Compose

Docker Compose runs every service from one file, which suits development and smaller production setups. Before you start, [install Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) with [Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/), and check the [requirements](#requirements).

1. In the directory that will hold your `docker-compose.yml`, create the egress CA for the sandbox. The sandbox reaches your Git platform only through a per-session proxy that adds the credentials, so the token never enters the sandbox, and the proxy signs with this CA:

   ```
   mkdir certs
   openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 3650 -subj "/CN=daiv-sandbox-egress" \
     -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" \
     -keyout certs/egress-ca.key -out certs/egress-ca.crt
   ```

1. Make the key readable, because the sandbox service runs as UID 1001:

   ```
   chmod 644 certs/egress-ca.key
   ```

1. Save the [Compose file](#compose-file) as `docker-compose.yml`, and replace each annotated value with your own. [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/index.md) lists the options.

1. Start the services:

   ```
   docker compose up -d --wait
   ```

   The command returns once every service is healthy. If one isn't, `docker compose logs <service>` shows why.

1. [Put DAIV behind Nginx](#put-daiv-behind-nginx), so you can reach it over HTTPS.

1. Create the first admin by running [`bootstrap_admin`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#bootstrap_admin), replacing `admin@example.com` with the admin's email address:

   ```
   docker compose exec app django-admin bootstrap_admin admin@example.com
   ```

1. Open `/accounts/login/` and sign in with the one-time code DAIV emails to that address.

If you turn on OAuth login before anyone signs in, the first Git platform sign-in becomes the admin instead. [The first admin](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#the-first-admin) explains both paths, and [Accounts and roles](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/index.md) covers adding users.

### Compose file

```
x-app-defaults: &x_app_default
  image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv:${DAIV_IMAGE_TAG:-main}
  restart: unless-stopped
  volumes:
    - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media # (1)!
  ulimits: # (2)!
    nofile:
      soft: 65536
      hard: 524288
  environment:
    DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: daiv.settings.production
    DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: secret-key # (3)!
    DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS: daiv.example.com,app,127.0.0.1 # (4)!
    DJANGO_REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
    DJANGO_REDIS_SESSION_URL: redis://redis:6379/1
    DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL: https://daiv.example.com # (5)!
    # Database settings
    DB_HOST: db
    DB_NAME: daiv
    DB_USER: daiv
    DB_PASSWORD: daivpass # (6)!
    DB_SSLMODE: prefer
    # Codebase settings
    CODEBASE_CLIENT: gitlab
    CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL: https://gitlab.com # (7)!
    CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN: gitlab-auth-token # (8)!
    CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET: gitlab-webhook-secret # (9)!
    # LLM Providers settings
    OPENROUTER_API_KEY: openrouter-api-key # (10)!
    # Email settings
    EMAIL_HOST: smtp.example.com # (11)!
    EMAIL_PORT: 587
    EMAIL_USE_TLS: true
    # Sandbox settings
    DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY: daiv-sandbox-api-key # (12)!
    # Optional: Git platform sign-in (OAuth). Setting these locks the fields at /dashboard/configuration/
    # ALLAUTH_CLIENT_ID: oauth-client-id
    # ALLAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: oauth-client-secret

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17.6
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: daiv
      POSTGRES_USER: daiv
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: daivpass # (13)!
    volumes:
      - db-volume:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U daiv -d daiv"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 30s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:8.6-alpine # (14)!
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - redis-volume:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  app:
    <<: *x_app_default
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    # volumes:  (15)
    #   - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media
    #   - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true
      sandbox:
        condition: service_healthy

  worker:
    <<: *x_app_default
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-worker default
    # volumes:  (15)
    #   - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media
    #   - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q 'db_worker' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    ports: []
    deploy:
      replicas: 1 # (16)!
    depends_on:
      app:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true

  worker-interactive:
    <<: *x_app_default
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-worker interactive
    # volumes:  (15)
    #   - media-volume:/home/daiv/data/media
    #   - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q 'db_worker' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    ports: []
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    depends_on:
      app:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true

  scheduler:
    <<: *x_app_default
    command: sh /home/daiv/start-crontask
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q 'crontask' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    ports: []
    depends_on:
      app:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true

  sandbox:
    image: ghcr.io/srtab/daiv-sandbox:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    group_add:
      - 987 # (17)!
    environment:
      DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY: daiv-sandbox-api-key # (18)!
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_CERT_FILE: /home/app/certs/egress-ca.crt
      DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_KEY_FILE: /home/app/certs/egress-ca.key
      DAIV_SANDBOX_REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/3
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ./certs:/home/app/certs:ro # (19)!

volumes:
  db-volume:
    driver: local
  redis-volume:
    driver: local
  media-volume:
    driver: local
```

1. **Required**: every service built from this anchor shares this directory. It holds the [artifacts](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/#artifacts) the agent publishes: `app` writes them for chat turns and serves them, and `worker` writes them for jobs and webhook runs.
1. **Raises the open-file limit** for every service built from this anchor. Each agent run holds many concurrent sockets (sandbox, LLM API, tracing, database, Redis, git over HTTPS), and Docker's default soft limit of 1024 open files fails under load with `[Errno 24] Too many open files`.
1. Generate a Django secret key, a long random string such as the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`.
1. Replace with your domain name, without the scheme (for example `daiv.example.com`). Keep `app` and `127.0.0.1` for communication between services.
1. Include the full URL with the scheme (for example `https://daiv.example.com`). Your GitLab sends webhooks to this URL, so it must be able to reach it.
1. Generate a random password for the database, such as the output of `openssl rand -hex 16`.
1. Set to your GitLab instance URL (for example `https://gitlab.com`).
1. The personal access token of DAIV's own GitLab user, with the `api` scope and the Maintainer role on your projects. Use a dedicated account: DAIV ignores comments written by the account its token belongs to. See [Platform setup](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/platform-setup/#gitlab-token-role-and-webhooks).
1. Generate a random webhook secret for GitLab webhook validation, such as the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`.
1. An OpenRouter API key for LLM access. DAIV copies it into its database on the first start. To change it later, edit the provider under **Configuration** → **Providers** in the dashboard; see [LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md).
1. The SMTP server DAIV sends sign-in codes through. Without one, replace the three `EMAIL_*` lines with `EMAIL_BACKEND: django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend` and read the codes from `docker compose logs app`.
1. Generate a random API key for the sandbox service, such as the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`.
1. Use the same password as in annotation 6.
1. Redis 8 or later; see [Requirements](#requirements).
1. **Optional**: uncomment the `volumes:` block of `app`, `worker` and `worker-interactive` to mount [custom global skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/#custom-global-skills) that are available across all repositories. `app` receives uploads from the dashboard, so it mounts the directory read-write; the workers run the agent, so they can mount it read-only. A service-level `volumes:` replaces the anchor's list instead of merging with it, so keep the `media-volume` line.
1. **Scaling**: increase `replicas` to handle more concurrent agent runs (for example `replicas: 3`). A worker runs one task to completion before it claims the next, so concurrency is the number of worker containers. Each claims independently from the queues named in its command.
1. Replace `987` with the group of the Docker socket, the output of `stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock`. The sandbox starts a container for each agent run through it.
1. Use the same API key as in annotation 12.
1. The egress CA from step 1 of [Deploy with Docker Compose](#deploy-with-docker-compose).

## Put DAIV behind Nginx

An Nginx reverse proxy gives your DAIV instance HTTPS access and domain routing. This page gives an Nginx configuration only; it has none for Apache, Traefik or other proxies.

DAIV needs HTTPS. Its session cookie, which also carries the CSRF token, is a secure cookie, so a browser keeps it only on `https://` URLs and on `localhost`. Over plain `http://` to any other address, sign-in fails with **CSRF verification failed**.

Before you start, [install Nginx](https://docs.nginx.com/nginx/admin-guide/installing-nginx/installing-nginx-open-source/), and have an SSL certificate for your domain and a domain name that points to your server.

1. Save the [Nginx configuration](#nginx-configuration) as `/etc/nginx/conf.d/daiv.conf`. The path may vary by operating system. Replace each annotated value with your own.

1. Restart Nginx:

   ```
   systemctl restart nginx
   ```

1. In a browser, open `https://daiv.example.com/accounts/login/`, replacing the domain with yours. You see the DAIV login page.

### Nginx configuration

```
upstream daiv-instance {
  server internal-ip:8000; # (1)!
}

server {
  listen              443 ssl;
  listen              [::]:443 ssl;

  http2               on;

  server_name         daiv.example.com; # (2)!

  # SSL Configuration.
  # You can use this https://ssl-config.mozilla.org/ to generate
  # the correct ssl configuration for your server.
  ssl_certificate      /etc/pki/tls/certs/ssl.crt; # (3)!
  ssl_certificate_key  /etc/pki/tls/private/ssl.key; # (4)!

  ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;
  ssl_ecdh_curve X25519:prime256v1:secp384r1;
  ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;

  location / {
    proxy_pass              http://daiv-instance;
    proxy_set_header        Host $host;
    proxy_set_header        X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header        X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_set_header        X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_redirect          off;
    proxy_buffering         off;
    proxy_connect_timeout   60;
    proxy_send_timeout      60;
    proxy_read_timeout      60;

    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000" always;
  }
}

server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    listen [::]:80;

    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}
```

1. Set the internal IP of your DAIV instance. Use `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` if Nginx runs on the same server.
1. Replace with your domain name (for example `daiv.example.com`).
1. Update the SSL certificate path. The location varies by operating system.
1. Update the SSL certificate key path. The location varies by operating system.

## Next steps

- **[Platform setup](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/platform-setup/index.md)** connects DAIV to your GitLab or GitHub repositories.
- **[LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md)** configures your LLM providers and API keys.
- **[Repository configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/index.md)** customizes DAIV's behavior per repository.
- **[Site configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/index.md)** manages settings from the dashboard instead of environment variables.
- **[MCP tools](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/mcp-tools/index.md)** connects the agent to external MCP servers.

# Platform setup

DAIV connects to one Git platform at a time, set by `CODEBASE_CLIENT`: GitLab (GitLab.com or self-managed) or GitHub (GitHub.com or GitHub Enterprise Server). Once connected, DAIV addresses labeled issues and reviews merge and pull requests in the repositories it can reach. Follow [Connect GitLab](#connect-gitlab) or [Connect GitHub](#connect-github).

## Connect GitLab

DAIV works as a GitLab user: it comments, pushes and opens merge requests as the user its token belongs to, and it ignores comments written by that user. Give DAIV its own account. With a token from your own account, DAIV ignores your comments, including the one that approves its plan.

You need:

- DAIV running, from [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md).

- Permission to add a member to each project DAIV works on.

- On GitLab.com, a second account for DAIV. On a self-managed instance, an admin to create the user.

- Create a GitLab user for DAIV, for example `daiv`. On GitLab.com, sign up a second account; on a self-managed instance, an admin creates it under **Admin** → **Users** → **New user**. The username is how you mention DAIV, for example `@daiv`.

- Add the user to each project DAIV works on, with the **Maintainer** role.

- Sign in to GitLab as the DAIV user.

- Select your avatar → **Edit profile** → **Access tokens**.

- Enter `DAIV Integration` as the token **Name**.

- Set the expiration according to your security policy.

- Select the `api` scope.

- Select **Create personal access token**.

  Warning

  GitLab shows the token once. Anyone who holds it acts as DAIV's user in every project that user belongs to. Store it in a secret manager, and never commit it to version control.

- Copy the token.

- If Deployment has not set a webhook secret, generate one. It is a random value that GitLab sends with each webhook for DAIV to validate. DAIV registers each webhook with the secret it already holds, so keep an existing one:

  ```
  openssl rand -hex 32
  ```

  Warning

  A Compose file holds the token and the webhook secret in plain text. Keep it out of version control, and readable only by the users who deploy DAIV.

- On Docker Compose, in the `environment` of `x-app-defaults` in your `docker-compose.yml`, set `CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL` to your GitLab URL (for example `https://gitlab.com`), `CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN` to the token and `CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to the webhook secret.

- On Docker Swarm, set `CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL` in `x-app-environment-defaults` of `stack.yml`.

- On Docker Swarm, check whether the `codebase_gitlab_auth_token` secret, which step 1 of [Deploy with Docker Swarm](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/#deploy-with-docker-swarm) created, already holds the token from step 9. If it does, skip to the redeploy step. Otherwise Docker cannot change it, so replace it with the next steps.

- On Docker Swarm, remove the stack: `docker stack rm daiv`.

- On Docker Swarm, remove the secret: `docker secret rm codebase_gitlab_auth_token`.

  Warning

  A value you type in a command is saved in your shell history and visible in the process list. Run the next command from a shell that does not record history.

- On Docker Swarm, create the secret again, replacing `<token>`:

  ```
  printf '%s' '<token>' | docker secret create codebase_gitlab_auth_token -
  ```

- Redeploy DAIV so it reads the values: `docker compose up -d` on Compose, or `docker stack deploy -c stack.yml daiv` on Swarm.

- Wait up to 5 minutes. DAIV's scheduler adds a webhook to each project where its user is a Maintainer or Owner. To add them at once, run [`setup_webhooks`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#setup_webhooks).

- In a project, open **Settings** → **Webhooks** and check for a webhook that points to `https://daiv.example.com/api/codebase/callbacks/gitlab/`, with the events in [GitLab token, role and webhooks](#gitlab-token-role-and-webhooks).

- Select **Test** → **Push events**, and check that GitLab reports a successful delivery.

- Create an issue titled "Add hello world function" in the project.

- Add the `daiv` label to the issue. If the project has no `daiv` label, create it from the label picker.

- Wait a few seconds. DAIV reacts with 👀, then comments with a plan.

- From your own account, comment on the issue mentioning DAIV's user, for example `@daiv proceed`. DAIV implements the plan and opens a merge request.

To change DAIV's behavior in a repository, add a `.daiv.yml` file to its root; [Repository configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/index.md) lists the options. [Issue addressing](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/issue-addressing/index.md) explains what DAIV does with an issue.

## GitLab token, role and webhooks

| Item             | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Token            | A personal access token of DAIV's user, with the `api` scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Role             | DAIV lists only the projects where its user is a Maintainer or Owner, and sets up webhooks on those.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Webhook URL      | `<DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL>/api/codebase/callbacks/gitlab/`. GitLab must be able to reach `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Webhook events   | Push events, Issues events, Comments (Note events), Merge request events and Pipeline events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Webhook creation | DAIV's scheduler runs `setup_webhooks` on the `CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON` schedule, every 5 minutes by default. See [Management commands](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#setup_webhooks) and [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/index.md). |

## Troubleshoot GitLab

### Webhook delivery fails

The webhook URL is not reachable from GitLab, or the certificate is invalid. Check that `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` is reachable from GitLab, that its SSL certificate is valid, and that no firewall blocks GitLab.

A self-managed GitLab refuses webhooks to private network addresses by default, with the error `Url is blocked: Requests to the local network are not allowed`. An admin allows them under **Admin** → **Settings** → **Network** → **Outbound requests**.

### DAIV ignores an issue

- The issue has no `daiv` label. Add it.
- DAIV's user is not a Maintainer or Owner of the project, so the project has no webhook. Change its role.
- `issue_addressing.enabled` is `false` in `.daiv.yml`. It is `true` by default.
- Check DAIV's logs for errors.

### DAIV ignores your comments

- DAIV ignores comments written by its own user. Comment from another account.
- Mention DAIV's username, for example `@daiv`.

### DAIV does not respond to merge request comments

- The webhook does not send **Comments (Note events)**. Run `setup_webhooks --update`.
- The webhook secret in GitLab does not match `CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. DAIV rejects the request.
- DAIV's user lacks access to the project.

### DAIV reports an error in a comment

DAIV comments "An unexpected error occurred" when a run fails. The worker and sandbox logs show why, for example `docker compose logs worker sandbox`.

## Connect GitHub

DAIV authenticates to GitHub as a GitHub App, which you create and install on the repositories DAIV works on. You need:

- DAIV running, from [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md).

- Permission to create and install a GitHub App on your account or organization.

- Open **Settings** → **Developer settings** → **GitHub Apps** in your account, or in **Organization Settings** for an organization.

- Select **New GitHub App**.

- Enter a unique name as the **GitHub App name**, for example `DAIV - <org-name>`, replacing `<org-name>` with your organization or account name. GitHub rejects a name another App uses.

- Enter your DAIV URL, for example `https://daiv.example.com`, as the **Homepage URL**.

- Enter `https://daiv.example.com/api/codebase/callbacks/github/` as the **Webhook URL**.

- Generate the webhook secret, and keep it for a later step:

  ```
  openssl rand -hex 32
  ```

- Enter the webhook secret as the **Webhook secret**.

  Warning

  The **Workflows** permission is optional, and it lets code that runs in the sandbox change files under `.github/workflows/`. Those workflows run with the repository's Actions secrets, which exposes the secrets to that code. Set it only if DAIV must push to those files.

- Set the repository permissions listed in [GitHub App permissions and events](#github-app-permissions-and-events).

- Subscribe the App to the events listed there.

- Select **Create GitHub App**.

  Warning

  The private key lets whoever holds it act as the App on every installed repository. GitHub offers the `.pem` file once, so store it where only DAIV's operators can read it.

- Under **Private keys**, select **Generate a private key**. Your browser downloads a `.pem` file.

- Copy the **App ID** from the top of the App's settings page.

- Select **Install App** in the left sidebar.

- Select your account or organization.

- Select **All repositories** or **Only select repositories**, and choose the repositories DAIV works on.

- Select **Install**.

- Copy the installation ID from the page's URL, `https://github.com/settings/installations/<installation-id>`.

- On Docker Compose, in the `environment` of `x-app-defaults` in your `docker-compose.yml`, set `CODEBASE_CLIENT: github`, `CODEBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID` to the App ID and `CODEBASE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID` to the installation ID. For GitHub Enterprise Server, also set `CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL`, for example `https://github.example.com`.

  Warning

  A Compose file holds the webhook secret in plain text. Keep it out of version control, and readable only by the users who deploy DAIV.

- On Docker Compose, set `CODEBASE_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the same `environment` to the webhook secret.

- On Docker Compose, add the private key as a file-based secret. Under `x-app-defaults`, add `secrets: [codebase_github_private_key]`. At the top level, add:

  ```
  secrets:
    codebase_github_private_key:
      file: <private-key-path>
  ```

  Replace `<private-key-path>` with the path of the `.pem` file. DAIV reads it from `/run/secrets/codebase_github_private_key`. The `secrets:` key in `x-app-defaults` reaches only the services that merge that anchor with `<<: *x_app_default`, which the [Compose file](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/#compose-file) does for `app`, `worker`, `worker-interactive` and `scheduler`. 21. On Docker Compose, give the `.pem` file to the user DAIV runs as, `daiv` with UID 1001, because Compose keeps the file's owner and permissions. Replace `<private-key-path>` with the path of the `.pem` file:

  ```
  sudo chown 1001:1001 <private-key-path>
  ```

- On Docker Compose, make the file readable by that user only:

  ```
  chmod 600 <private-key-path>
  ```

- On Docker Swarm, in `x-app-environment-defaults` of `stack.yml`, set `CODEBASE_CLIENT: github`, `CODEBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID` and `CODEBASE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID`. For GitHub Enterprise Server, also set `CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL`.

  Warning

  A value you type in a command is saved in your shell history and visible in the process list. Run the next command from a shell that does not record history, or from a script that reads the value from a protected file.

- On Docker Swarm, create the webhook secret, replacing `<webhook-secret>`:

  ```
  printf '%s' '<webhook-secret>' | docker secret create codebase_github_webhook_secret -
  ```

- On Docker Swarm, create the private key secret from the `.pem` file, replacing `<private-key-path>`:

  ```
  docker secret create codebase_github_private_key <private-key-path>
  ```

- On Docker Swarm, add `codebase_github_private_key` and `codebase_github_webhook_secret` to the `secrets:` list of `app`, `worker`, `worker-interactive` and `scheduler`, and declare both under the top-level `secrets:` with `external: true`, as the stack file does for the other secrets.

- Redeploy DAIV so it reads the values: `docker compose up -d` on Compose, or `docker stack deploy -c stack.yml daiv` on Swarm.

- Create an issue titled "Add hello world function" in a repository where you installed the App.

- Add the `daiv` label to the issue. If the repository has no `daiv` label, create it.

- Wait a few seconds. DAIV comments with a plan.

- In your GitHub App's settings, open **Advanced** → **Recent Deliveries**, and check that the `issues` delivery for the test issue shows a `204` response. The `ping` and `installation` deliveries from before DAIV was configured show an error, and you can ignore them.

To change DAIV's behavior in a repository, add a `.daiv.yml` file to its root; [Repository configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/index.md) lists the options. [Issue addressing](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/issue-addressing/index.md) explains what DAIV does with an issue.

## GitHub App permissions and events

GitHub sends the events of every repository that has the App installed to the one webhook set on the App. DAIV does not create webhooks on GitHub, and [`setup_webhooks`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#setup_webhooks) does nothing there.

| Repository permission | Access                  | DAIV uses it to                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contents              | Read & Write            | Create branches and commits.                                                                                           |
| Issues                | Read & Write            | Read and comment on issues.                                                                                            |
| Pull requests         | Read & Write            | Create and update pull requests.                                                                                       |
| Actions               | Read-only               | Read workflow runs and job logs for [pipeline watch](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/pipeline-watch/index.md). |
| Workflows             | Read & Write (optional) | Push changes to files under `.github/workflows/`, such as a conflict resolved there.                                   |
| Metadata              | Read-only               | GitHub selects it for you.                                                                                             |

Subscribe the App to these events:

- **Push**
- **Issues**
- **Issue comment**
- **Pull request review comment**, for mentions and comments on diff lines of a pull request a DAIV session owns
- **Pull request**
- **Workflow run**, which GitHub lists only once **Actions** is **Read-only**

If you grant a new permission to an App that is already installed, each installation owner must accept it. Until they do, the features that need it do not run on that installation.

## Troubleshoot GitHub

### Webhook delivery fails

- Check that `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` is reachable from GitHub and has a valid SSL certificate.
- Check that the **Webhook secret** in the GitHub App matches `CODEBASE_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Without a match, DAIV answers 401.
- Check that `CODEBASE_CLIENT` is `github`. Otherwise DAIV answers 403.
- A `ping` or `installation` delivery fails even when DAIV is configured, because it has no repository. DAIV answers 422. Check the `issues` delivery instead.
- Check DAIV's logs for the incoming requests.

### DAIV ignores an issue

- The issue has no `daiv` label. Add it.
- The App lacks the **Issues** permission with **Read & Write** access.
- `issue_addressing.enabled` is `false` in `.daiv.yml`. It is `true` by default.
- Check DAIV's logs for errors.

### DAIV does not respond to comments

- The App is not subscribed to **Issue comment**, **Pull request review comment** or both. See [GitHub App permissions and events](#github-app-permissions-and-events).
- The App is not installed on the repository.

### DAIV fails to start with permission denied on the private key

The log shows `permission denied` on `/run/secrets/codebase_github_private_key`. The `.pem` file is not readable by UID 1001. Run `sudo chown 1001:1001 <private-key-path>` and `chmod 600 <private-key-path>`, then restart DAIV.

### Authentication fails

- The private key is not in PEM format, or lacks its header and footer lines.
- `CODEBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID` or `CODEBASE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID` is wrong.
- The App is not installed on the repositories DAIV works on.

## Next steps

- **[LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md)** configures your LLM provider and API keys.
- **[Repository configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/index.md)** customizes DAIV's behavior per repository.
- **[Issue addressing](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/issue-addressing/index.md)** explains how DAIV handles issues.
- **[Pull request assistant](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/pull-request-assistant/index.md)** explains how DAIV reviews code.

# Accounts and roles

DAIV's web dashboard requires you to sign in. Every signed-in user has one of two roles, **admin** or **member**, which decide what they can see and change. Members manage their own work: agent runs, chats, schedules and API keys. Admins also manage the deployment: users, site configuration, schedule templates, skills, and global MCP servers and sandbox environments.

DAIV does not offer email-and-password signup. Signup through your Git platform is off by default: an admin turns it on with **Open social signup**, described in [Turn on OAuth login](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#turn-on-oauth-login). Otherwise an admin creates each user, who then signs in with a one-time email code, a passkey, or the Git platform account when OAuth login is on.

## Roles

DAIV has two roles. New users are members.

| Capability                                                                                        | Member                                                                            | Admin                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Start and view agent runs and chats                                                               | On the repositories they can access (see [Repository access](#repository-access)) | On every repository             |
| Create and view [scheduled jobs](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/scheduled-jobs/index.md) | Their own, on repositories they can write to                                      | Everyone's, on every repository |
| Create API keys                                                                                   | Their own                                                                         | Their own                       |
| Revoke API keys                                                                                   | Their own                                                                         | Any user's key                  |
| Manage notification channels                                                                      | Their own                                                                         | Their own                       |
| **Users**: create, edit and delete users                                                          | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| **Configuration**: edit the site configuration                                                    | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| **Schedule templates**: create, edit and delete them                                              | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| **Skills**: open the skills dashboard                                                             | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| **Global MCP servers**: manage the servers every user gets                                        | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| Create and change global sandbox environments                                                     | No                                                                                | Yes                             |
| Consolidate a repository's memory on demand                                                       | No                                                                                | Yes                             |

The admin-only pages are under **Admin** in the sidebar's **Settings** menu, the cog beside your account.

## Repository access

A member sees and acts on a repository only when they have access to it on the connected Git platform, GitLab or GitHub. DAIV mirrors each user's repository membership from the platform and checks it before it shows or runs anything on a repository. There is no separate DAIV-side permission to manage. Admins skip these checks.

DAIV checks two tiers, matched to the platform's own roles:

| Tier      | Required platform role                                           | Gates                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Read**  | GitLab Reporter or above, GitHub read (or higher) collaborator   | Repository and branch pickers, the [memory dashboard](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/memory/index.md), and the MCP `list_repositories` tool.                               |
| **Write** | GitLab Developer or above, GitHub write (or higher) collaborator | Starting an agent run or chat, and creating or running a [scheduled job](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/scheduled-jobs/index.md), from the dashboard, the Jobs API or MCP. |

A repository a user cannot read never appears in a listing. A repository they can read but not write to appears, and DAIV rejects their run, chat and schedule attempts with a "not accessible" message.

DAIV learns what a user can access on the platform only after that user signs in with their Git platform account once, and matches the platform account to the DAIV user by email. A user an admin created, who has only ever signed in with an email code, has no repository access until they sign in with GitLab or GitHub once.

A periodic sync copies repository membership from the platform, so a permission change on the platform takes effect at the next sync, not immediately. [Git platform](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#git-platform) gives the sync schedule and how long DAIV keeps trusting access data after a sync fails.

## Sign in

The login page is at `/accounts/login/`. A user signs in with any of these methods:

- **Email code.** Works without further setup, as long as DAIV can send email.
- **Git platform account.** Works once an admin has turned on OAuth login.
- **Passkey.** Works once the user has added one.

### Sign in with an email code

DAIV emails a one-time code that signs a user in without a password. Admin-created users and the first admin use this method.

1. On the login page, enter your email address and select **Continue with email**.
1. Read the code in the email DAIV sends. The code expires after 5 minutes and accepts 3 attempts.
1. Enter the code and select **Verify & sign in**.

Without an SMTP server, set `EMAIL_BACKEND` to `django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend` and read the code from the app's log with `docker compose logs app`. [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#authentication) lists the email settings.

### Sign in with GitHub or GitLab

DAIV offers the platform it is connected to, **GitHub** or **GitLab** including a self-managed GitLab, and never both at once. On the login page, select **Continue with GitHub** or **Continue with GitLab**.

With **Open social signup** off, create each permitted user under **Admin** → **Users** with the email address their Git platform account confirms. For GitLab, DAIV checks the profile's `confirmed_at` to verify that this primary email address is confirmed before it looks up an existing account. Matching ignores case and keeps the existing user's role. If GitLab sends no confirmation or an invalid one, DAIV does not link the account by email. An account already linked to a platform user ID stays linked when the platform email changes.

DAIV checks again, before it saves a new account, that signup is open. A pending signup form cannot create a second user by replacing an email address that already exists.

To turn on Git platform sign-in, [create the OAuth app](#create-the-oauth-app), then follow [Turn on OAuth login](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#turn-on-oauth-login).

### Sign in with a passkey

A passkey is Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello or a security key. After a user signs in, they add one under **Passkeys** in the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar. On the login page they then select **Sign in with a passkey**. Email sign-in stays available, so a lost passkey does not lock the user out.

### Create the OAuth app

Create an OAuth app on your Git platform to get the client ID and client secret that DAIV needs for OAuth login. You need an account that can create the app on that platform, and the URL DAIV is served from (`DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`), for example `https://daiv.example.com`.

To create the app on GitHub:

1. Open [github.com/settings/developers](https://github.com/settings/developers).
1. Select **OAuth Apps** → **New OAuth App**.
1. In **Application name**, enter a name, for example `DAIV`.
1. In **Homepage URL**, enter your DAIV URL, for example `https://daiv.example.com`.
1. In **Authorization callback URL**, enter your DAIV URL followed by `/accounts/github/login/callback/`, for example `https://daiv.example.com/accounts/github/login/callback/`.
1. Select **Register application**.
1. Copy the **Client ID**.
1. Select **Generate a new client secret**, and copy the secret.

To create the app on GitLab:

1. Open **Admin Area** → **Applications** or **User Settings** → **Applications**.
1. Add a new application.
1. In **Name**, enter a name, for example `DAIV`.
1. In **Redirect URI**, enter your DAIV URL followed by `/accounts/gitlab/login/callback/`, for example `https://daiv.example.com/accounts/gitlab/login/callback/`.
1. Under **Scopes**, select `read_user`.
1. Select **Save application**.
1. Copy the **Application ID** and the **Secret**.

Enter the client ID and secret under **Configuration** → **Authentication**, where DAIV calls the secret **Auth Client Secret**: [Turn on OAuth login](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#turn-on-oauth-login) gives the steps, and [Authentication](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#authentication) lists the variables that override the same fields and lock them.

## The first admin

A new DAIV install has no users, so it has no admin. Two paths create the first one: the first Git platform sign-in, and a command in a shell.

### Make the first OAuth sign-in the admin

With OAuth login on and no user in DAIV, the first person who signs in with the Git platform account gets an account even when **Open social signup** is off, and DAIV makes them an admin. DAIV makes a new account an admin whenever the install has no admin, not whenever it has no user. If two people sign in at the same moment, both become admins rather than neither.

### Create the first admin from a shell

Use this path when OAuth login is off. The [`bootstrap_admin`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#bootstrap_admin) command refuses to run if an admin already exists, or if a user with that email already exists: promote that user from **Users** instead.

1. Run the command, replacing `admin@example.com` with the admin's email address:

   ```
   docker compose exec app django-admin bootstrap_admin admin@example.com
   ```

1. [Sign in with an email code](#sign-in-with-an-email-code) as that address.

[Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md) covers the first-run setup, including email.

## Manage users

Admins manage users under **Admin** → **Users**, at `/accounts/users/`. The list searches by name or email address and filters by role.

### Create a user

1. Under **Admin** → **Users**, select **Create user**.
1. In **Name**, **Email** and **Role**, enter the user's details.
1. Select **Create user**.

DAIV emails the user a welcome message with a sign-in link. The new account has no password: the user signs in with an email code, a passkey, or the Git platform account.

### Edit a user

1. Under **Admin** → **Users**, select the user.
