| `orchestration`          | `enabled`      | `true`    | [Orchestration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/orchestration/index.md): let the agent delegate sub-jobs to other repositories, or to new sessions on this one.                              |
| `memory`                 | `enabled`      | `true`    | Repository memory: capture observations from finished runs, consolidate them, and add them to the system prompt of later runs. Set it to `false` to opt this repository out.                         |

`pipeline_watch.enabled` and `memory.enabled` apply only while the matching site-wide setting is on too: **Pipeline Watch** and **Memory** in [Site configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/index.md). The other toggles apply to the repository alone.

## Model overrides

A repository can use different models from the site's, for example smaller models on simple projects and larger ones on complex projects. A model is written as a model spec such as `openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`; see [LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md).

The model for a run comes from the first source in this list that sets one, highest priority first:

1. **A model picked for the run**, in the agent picker or as `agent_model` through the API and MCP.
1. **The `daiv-max` issue label**, described in [Issue addressing](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/issue-addressing/#max-mode). Max mode uses the site's max thinking level, not `thinking_level`.
1. **The `models` section of `.daiv.yml`.**
1. **Site settings**: environment variables or the Site Configuration page.

DAIV tries the model from the highest source that sets one first. The `models.agent` model and fallback follow it, or the site's models where the file sets none.

### Agent

The main DAIV agent handles issue addressing, pull request assistance and all interactive tasks.

| Option                        | Type                                                          | Default      | Description                               |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `models.agent.model`          | `str`                                                         | site setting | Primary model.                            |
| `models.agent.fallback_model` | `str`                                                         | site setting | Fallback if the primary model fails.      |
| `models.agent.thinking_level` | `"minimal" \| "low" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "xhigh" \| null` | site setting | Thinking depth. Set to `null` to disable. |

A model picked for a single run is tried first, with the model and fallback above after it, and a thinking level picked for a run beats `thinking_level`.

### Diff to metadata

The diff to metadata agent generates pull request titles, descriptions and commit messages from diffs.

| Option                                   | Type  | Default      | Description                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `models.diff_to_metadata.model`          | `str` | site setting | Primary model.                       |
| `models.diff_to_metadata.fallback_model` | `str` | site setting | Fallback if the primary model fails. |

### Skill and subagent models

Run a skill or a subagent on a chosen model in this repository, by name. An entry overrides the site's entry for the same name only; every other site entry still applies. Site entries are set in the dashboard: a skill's on the **Models** tab of its page, which also holds the code-review detectors', and the general-purpose and explore subagents' under **Configuration** → **Agent**.

| Option                    | Type          | Default    | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `models.skills.<name>`    | `str \| null` | site entry | Model for the skill's model calls, from its invocation until your next message. |
| `models.subagents.<name>` | `str \| null` | site entry | Model for every call the subagent makes.                                        |

```
models:
  skills:
    code-review: "openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5"
    plan: null   # unset: the site entry, if any, applies
  subagents:
    cr-security: "openrouter:anthropic/claude-opus-5.5"
    my-repo-subagent: "openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.2"
```

Replace `<name>` with the name of a skill or subagent. For a given name, the model resolves in this order, first match wins:

1. this repository's entry;
1. the site's entry (a skill page's **Models** tab, or **Configuration** → **Agent** → **Subagent models**);
1. the model the subagent file, or a built-in or global skill file, declares (a repository skill's `metadata.model` is ignored);
1. the run's model.

A model picked for the run, `daiv-max`, or an exact model passed to the jobs API does not override these entries. Configured models run with the run's thinking level.

DAIV checks the values when a run uses them, not when the file loads, so a typo never drops the rest of `.daiv.yml`. An entry that can't be used falls back to the model the file declares, else the run's model, not to the site entry, and DAIV logs the failure as an error. Names that match no skill or subagent are ignored. See [Agent skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/#run-a-skill-on-another-model) and [Subagents](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/#subagent-model-precedence).

# Agent skills

Skills are modular capabilities that extend DAIV's agent with specialized knowledge and workflows. Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file with instructions the agent follows when the skill is triggered.

DAIV ships with [built-in skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/slash-commands/#built-in-skills). You can also write your own, for one repository or for all of them.

## How skills work

Skills use a **progressive disclosure** pattern:

1. **At startup**, DAIV reads the `name` and `description` from each skill's YAML frontmatter (about 100 tokens per skill).
1. **When triggered**, DAIV reads the full `SKILL.md` content and follows its instructions.
1. **As needed**, the agent reads the supporting files bundled with the skill (scripts, templates, configs).

This keeps context usage minimal until a skill is needed.

## Directory structure

Skills can live in any of these directories at the repository root:

- `.agents/skills/`
- `.claude/skills/`
- `.cursor/skills/`

DAIV scans all three. When more than one holds a skill with the same name, `.agents/skills/` wins over `.claude/skills/`, which wins over `.cursor/skills/`.

```
my-repository/
├── .agents/
│   └── skills/
│       └── my-custom-skill/
│           ├── SKILL.md           # Required
│           └── scripts/
│               └── helper.py      # Optional supporting files
└── src/
```

DAIV does not copy built-in skills into your repository, and writes nothing to `.agents/skills/`. It loads them from its own global skills location (`/workspace/skills` inside the agent), a separate source next to the per-repository directories.

## Override priority

DAIV resolves a skill name in this order, highest priority first:

1. **Per-repository skills**, committed in the repository's `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` or `.cursor/skills/`.
1. **Custom global skills**, [mounted from the host or uploaded in the dashboard](#custom-global-skills).
1. **Built-in skills**, shipped with DAIV.

A custom global skill overrides the built-in skill of the same name, and a per-repository skill overrides both. To override a built-in skill in one repository, commit a skill with the same name to that repository.

The agent's system prompt lists the global source as `Global Skills`, and marks the last source, `.agents/skills`, `(higher priority)`.

## Skill security

Use skills from trusted sources only

Skills give the agent instructions and access to scripts. Use only skills you wrote or got from a source you trust.

Before you commit or upload a skill:

- Audit every file in it.
- Review its scripts carefully, because the agent can run any executable code in a skill.
- Check its external references, because a skill that fetches data from external URLs adds risk.

## Create a skill

To add a skill to one repository, create a directory for it and commit it. You need write access to the repository.

1. In `.agents/skills/` at the repository root, create a directory named after the skill, with lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (for example `changelog`).
1. In that directory, create `SKILL.md`.
1. Add the YAML frontmatter with a `name` that matches the directory name and a `description`.
1. Below the frontmatter, write the instructions the agent follows.
1. Optional: add supporting files next to `SKILL.md`, such as scripts or templates.
1. Commit the directory to the repository.

DAIV loads the skill in runs on a branch that contains it. To have the agent walk you through these steps instead, run `@daiv /skill-creator` (see [`/skill-creator`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/slash-commands/#skill-creator)).

### SKILL.md format

Every skill requires a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter:

```
---
name: my-skill
description: Brief description of what this skill does and when the agent should use it
---

# My Skill

## Instructions

1. First, do this
2. Then, do that
3. Finally, verify the result
```

Required fields:

| Field         | Constraints                                                                     | Description                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | Max 64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, must match the directory name | Unique identifier for the skill. This is what users type after `/`.                                                        |
| `description` | Max 1024 chars                                                                  | What the skill does **and when to use it**. The agent matches user requests against this text, so include trigger phrases. |

Optional fields:

| Field           | Description                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `license`       | License name or reference to a bundled license file           |
| `compatibility` | Environment requirements (max 500 chars)                      |
| `metadata`      | Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional properties           |
| `allowed-tools` | Space-delimited list of tool names the skill recommends using |

### Write a good description

The `description` field is how the agent decides whether to use your skill. Include specific trigger phrases:

```
# Good: includes trigger phrases the agent can match
description: >
  Diagnose and fix CI/CD pipeline failures. Use when the user mentions
  "pipeline is failing", "CI broken", "fix the build", or "debug the tests".

# Bad: too vague for the agent to match
description: Helps with CI/CD issues.
```

### Write specific instructions

Tell the agent exactly what steps to follow:

```
## Instructions

1. Fetch the merge request diff using the platform tools
2. For each changed file, check for:
   - Missing error handling
   - Unvalidated inputs
   - Hardcoded credentials
3. Report findings grouped by severity (High / Medium / Low)
```

### Bundle supporting files

Skills can include helper scripts, templates and reference documents. Reference them by paths relative to the skill directory:

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md
├── scripts/
│   └── validate.py
└── templates/
    └── report.md
```

```
## Resources
- Run `scripts/validate.py` to check prerequisites
- Use `templates/report.md` as the output format
```

## Example: changelog skill

````
---
name: changelog
description: >
  Update the CHANGELOG.md file when changes are made. Use when the user
  asks to "update the changelog", "add a changelog entry", or after
  completing a feature implementation.
---

# Changelog Maintenance

## Instructions

1. Read `CHANGELOG.md` from the repository root
2. Determine the change type: Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed
3. Add an entry under the `## Unreleased` section
4. Follow the existing format and style in the file
5. Keep entries concise: one line per change

## Format

Use [Common Changelog](https://common-changelog.org/) format:

```markdown
## Unreleased

### Added
- New feature description
````

```

## Set branch and commit conventions

DAIV generates the branch names and commit messages for its changes. To make it follow your conventions, describe them in the repository's context file: `AGENTS.md`, or the file that `context_file_name` names in [`.daiv.yml`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/#repository-settings). `.daiv.yml` has no option for the conventions themselves.

1. Open the context file in the repository root.
2. Add a section for each convention you want DAIV to follow.
3. Commit the file.

For example:

```

## Branch naming

Use: pr/<issue-id>-<kebab-summary>

## Commit messages

Use: (<ISSUE-ID>) <type>: <summary> Where <type> is one of: feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test

```

The angle-bracket parts belong to the convention: DAIV fills in the issue ID, type and summary for each change.

Without a convention, DAIV names branches `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>` and writes commit subjects in the Conventional Commits style, `<type>: <short summary>`, with a type of feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor or test.

## Custom global skills

A custom global skill is available in **all repositories**, unlike a per-repository skill. It has the same format as a built-in skill, a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file, and DAIV loads it from a directory on the host. You put skills there in one of two ways:

- [Mount a directory](#mount-a-directory-of-global-skills) of skills into the containers.
- [Upload a ZIP archive](#upload-a-global-skill) in the dashboard, as an admin.

Both use the same directory, `DAIV_AGENT_CUSTOM_SKILLS_PATH`, once it is mounted into the `app` container and into every container that runs the agent, so you can use both. A mounted skill appears in runs but not on the **Skills** page, which lists only uploaded skills.

DAIV materializes the skills at each agent invocation, so a new skill or a new file takes effect on the next task without a container restart. DAIV does not pick up an edit to a file it has already loaded, so replace the skill by upload, or recreate the containers that run the agent after editing a mounted file. A plain restart is not enough, because the cache lives in the container's `/tmp`. With Docker Compose, run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate worker worker-interactive`. With Docker Swarm, run `docker service update --force <stack>_worker` and `docker service update --force <stack>_worker-interactive`, replacing `<stack>` with your stack name.

### Mount a directory of global skills

1. On the host, create a directory with your skills, one subdirectory per skill:

```

custom-skills/ ├── my-workflow/ │ ├── SKILL.md │ └── scripts/ │ └── helper.py └── team-review/ └── SKILL.md

```
2. In your `docker-compose.yml` or `stack.yml`, mount the directory at `/home/daiv/data/skills` into `app`, which receives dashboard uploads and needs it read-write, and into `worker` and `worker-interactive`, which run the agent and can mount it read-only:

```

app: volumes: - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills worker: volumes: - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro worker-interactive: volumes: - ./custom-skills:/home/daiv/data/skills:ro

```
3. Recreate the three containers.

A service-level `volumes:` replaces the list it inherits, so keep each service's existing `media-volume` line (see [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md)). To mount the directory elsewhere, set `DAIV_AGENT_CUSTOM_SKILLS_PATH` (see [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#daiv-agent)).

### Upload a global skill

An upload replaces a skill of the same name

If a custom skill with the same name exists, uploading replaces it for every repository. DAIV moves the old version to `.trash/` under `DAIV_AGENT_CUSTOM_SKILLS_PATH` and removes it on the next upload or delete after 24 hours.

You need an admin account and a ZIP archive that meets the [ZIP requirements](#zip-requirements).

1. In the sidebar, select **Settings** → **Skills**.
2. Select **Upload skill**.
3. Under **Skill zip**, choose the ZIP archive.
4. Select **Upload**.
5. If DAIV shows **Replace existing skill**, choose the ZIP archive again and select **Replace**.

The skill appears under **Custom skills**. DAIV records which admin uploaded it.

#### ZIP requirements

DAIV validates the archive before it stores it:

| Constraint | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Top-level directory | Exactly one, named after the skill (a valid slug: lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, max 63 chars) |
| `SKILL.md` | Required at `<skill-name>/SKILL.md`, with `name` (matching the directory) and `description` in its frontmatter |
| Compressed size | 5 MiB max |
| Unpacked size | 25 MiB max |
| File count | 200 max |
| Path depth | 8 levels max |
| Per-file size | 1 MiB max |
| Allowed file types | `.md`, `.py`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.txt`, `.sh`, `.toml`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.svg`, `.gif` |

DAIV rejects symlinks, absolute paths, `..` path traversal and hidden path segments. It drops `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, `.git` and `.gitignore` entries silently.

### Manage global skills in the dashboard

The **Skills** page needs an admin account. **Custom skills** lists the skills uploaded in the dashboard, and **Built-in skills** lists the ones DAIV ships. Each card shows the skill's invocation count and, when its entry names one, its model. A custom skill whose name matches a built-in skill shadows it, and its card carries an **Overrides built-in** warning icon. A skill that you only mounted loads in runs but has no card or page, so it cannot be downloaded or deleted here.

Select a skill to open its page, which has four tabs:

- **SKILL.md**: the skill's instructions.
- **Files**: the files in the skill.
- **Models**: the model the skill runs on (see [Run a skill on another model](#run-a-skill-on-another-model)).
- **Usage**: the invocations over the last 30 days, and the latest runs that invoked the skill, each linking to its run in its session.

To download a custom skill's original ZIP archive, select **Download zip** on its card menu or its page.

#### Delete a custom skill

Deleting removes the skill from every repository

DAIV moves the skill to a recycle bin for 24 hours before it removes it permanently. Download the ZIP archive first if you may need it. A custom skill that shadowed a built-in skill stops doing so: the built-in skill applies again.

You cannot delete a built-in skill.

1. On the **Skills** page, find the skill under **Custom skills**.
2. Open its card menu and select **Delete**.
3. Select **Delete skill**.

## Run a skill on another model

Once the agent invokes a skill, its model calls run on the skill's model until your next message. The model comes from the skill's `models.skills` entry in the repository's `.daiv.yml`, else its entry on the **Models** tab or in `DAIV_AGENT_SKILL_MODELS`, else the skill file's `metadata.model`, else the run's model. [Skill and subagent models](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/#skill-and-subagent-models) gives the order and the entry format.

The **Models** tab changes a skill's model for every repository, built-in skills included, without copying or editing the skill file. On `/code-review` it also sets the model of each detector the skill ships (see [Subagent model precedence](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/#subagent-model-precedence)). A skill that exists only in repositories, or that you only mounted, has no page: give it a model with `DAIV_AGENT_SKILL_MODELS`, or with a `models.skills` entry in each repository's `.daiv.yml`.

A built-in or global skill file can name its own model in `metadata.model`, as a model spec (`provider-slug:model`, as in [subagents](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/index.md)):

```

______________________________________________________________________

## name: changelog description: Update CHANGELOG.md for the current changes. metadata: model: openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

````

DAIV ignores a repository skill's `metadata.model`, because the file comes from the branch the run works on, which the author of a merge request controls.

The run's thinking level carries over. The run's model serves any model call whose conversation no longer fits the skill model's context window. Once the skill model fails a call, the run's model serves that call and every later one in the run, before the run's fallback models. Switching models starts a fresh prompt cache on each side, so a cheaper skill model pays off only for skills that do substantial work.

When a configured entry names a provider that is unknown, disabled or missing its API key, the skill runs on its `metadata.model`, else the run's model, and DAIV logs the failure at ERROR. A `metadata.model` that DAIV can't use keeps the run's model, logged the same way.```
````

# MCP tools

[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) tools extend DAIV's agent with access to external services. You manage MCP servers from the dashboard on two pages:

- **MCP Servers**, in the sidebar's **Settings** menu as **MCP servers**, shows your personal servers and a read-only list of the global servers that load in every run.
- **Global MCP Servers**, in the sidebar's **Settings** menu under **Admin** as **Global MCP servers**, is where admins manage the built-in and custom global servers.

The DAIV app opens the connections itself at runtime, so no sidecar containers are required. DAIV skips a server that does not return its tools within the load timeout (see [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#mcp-tools)).

## Server settings

Each server is a row with these settings:

| Setting         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Name**        | Unique slug of lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 80 characters. You cannot change it after you create the server. `new` and `test` are reserved.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Description** | Optional text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Status**      | **Active** loads the server in every run (for a personal server, every run that acts as its owner). **On-demand** loads it only in runs that opt in, for example with `mcp_overrides` in the [jobs API](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/jobs-api/#request-fields). **Disabled** never loads it. |
| **Transport**   | **HTTP (streamable)** or **SSE**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **URL**         | The MCP endpoint, an `http` or `https` URL of up to 200 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Headers**     | HTTP headers sent to the server. Each header is a literal value, encrypted at rest, or an `env_ref`, the name of an environment variable that DAIV resolves at runtime.                                                                                                                                 |
| **Tool filter** | Which of the server's tools the agent sees (see [Tool filtering](#tool-filtering)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

There is no scope field on the form: the page you create the server from decides it.

The **Tool filter** section is hidden until it has something to act on. On a new server it appears after a successful **Test connection**. On an existing server it appears once DAIV has synced the server's tools, or when a filter is active. The **Refresh tools** button next to the heading syncs the tools again, and the heading shows when the last sync ran and how many tools it found.

### Tool filtering

Set **Tool filter mode** to one of:

- **None**: the agent sees all the server's tools.
- **Allow only listed tools**: the agent sees only the listed tools.
- **Block listed tools**: the agent sees all tools except the listed ones.

A filter other than **None** needs at least one tool name. An allow-list fails closed: a tool that disappears upstream stops being exposed.

## Security

MCP connections bypass the sandbox egress proxy

MCP connections originate from the DAIV app and worker containers, so the sandbox egress proxy does not apply to them. Restrict outbound access at your network layer if you need to.

- DAIV encrypts header values at rest and never renders them back into the form. An `env_ref` header keeps the value out of the database entirely.
- Prefer allow-lists that exclude tools that change data, as the seeded Sentry filter does.

## Built-in servers

DAIV seeds two built-in servers that point at the official remote MCP endpoints. You can edit a built-in server's URL, headers and tool filter, but you cannot rename or delete it, only disable it.

| Server     | URL                                                                      | Status                                                       | Tool filter                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sentry`   | `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp?disable-skills=seer,docs,project-management` | **Disabled**, because the endpoint requires authentication   | **Allow only listed tools**, with read-only tools only             |
| `context7` | `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`                                           | **Active**, and works without credentials at low rate limits | **Allow only listed tools**: `resolve-library-id` and `query-docs` |

### Enable the Sentry server

You need an admin account and a [Sentry User Auth Token](https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/) with the read scopes `org:read`, `project:read`, `team:read` and `event:read`.

1. In the sidebar, select **Settings** → **Global MCP servers**.
1. Under **Built-in**, select **Edit** on the `sentry` server.
1. Under **Headers**, select **Add header**.
1. Enter `Authorization` as the header name.
1. Enter `Sentry-Bearer <your token>` as the value, and leave the mode as `literal`.
1. Select **Test connection**. DAIV reports how many tools it discovered.
1. Optional: under **Tool filter**, adjust which tools the agent sees.
1. Under **Status**, select **Active**.
1. Select **Save**.

Replace `<your token>` with your Sentry token. `Sentry-Bearer`, not `Bearer`, is Sentry's scheme for passing an API token directly to its hosted MCP. To keep the token out of the database, set the header's mode to `env_ref` and enter the name of an environment variable that holds the whole `Sentry-Bearer <your token>` string.

### Raise the `context7` rate limits

You need an admin account and an API key from [context7.com/dashboard](https://context7.com/dashboard).

1. In the sidebar, select **Settings** → **Global MCP servers**.
1. Under **Built-in**, select **Edit** on the `context7` server.
1. Under **Headers**, select **Add header**.
1. Enter `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` as the header name.
1. Enter your API key as the value.
1. Select **Save**.

## Add a server

You can add any server that DAIV reaches over HTTP or SSE. A server that only speaks stdio needs a [bridge](#stdio-only-servers) first. Any member can add a personal server. Only admins can add a global one.

1. In the sidebar's **Settings** menu, open the page for the server's scope: **MCP servers** for a personal server, or, as an admin, **Global MCP servers** under **Admin** for a global one.
1. Select **New server**.
1. Enter a **Name**.
1. Choose a **Transport**.
1. Enter the **URL**.
1. Optional: select **Add header** and enter each header's name, mode and value.
1. Select **Test connection**. DAIV reports how many tools it discovered.
1. Optional: under **Tool filter**, choose a **Tool filter mode** and select the tools.
1. Set **Status**.
1. Select **Save**.

**Test connection** fails after 5 seconds. A personal server's headers are always literal (see [Personal servers](#personal-servers)).

## Stdio-only servers

DAIV connects over HTTP and SSE only. To use a stdio-based MCP server, wrap it with a stdio-to-HTTP bridge in its own container, then [add the bridge's URL](#add-a-server) as a server. Run one bridge container per MCP server, so a failure in one does not affect another.

## Connect an on-premise Sentry

Sentry's hosted MCP serves only sentry.io. The official [`@sentry/mcp-server`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sentry/mcp-server) package is stdio-only, so for a self-hosted Sentry you expose it over HTTP yourself and point the `sentry` server's URL at it. You have two options.

### Bridge the stdio package

Any stdio-to-HTTP bridge works. This example uses [supergateway](https://github.com/supercorp-ai/supergateway).

Run the bridge in stateful mode

Pass `--stateful`. In stateless mode every tool call starts a fresh child process chain, which can exhaust the system's thread limit under concurrent load. Pass `--sessionTimeout` in milliseconds (`300000` works well) to clean up idle sessions.

1. Add the bridge to your Compose file:

   ```
   mcp-sentry:
     image: supercorp/supergateway:latest
     restart: unless-stopped
     command:
       - --stdio
       - "npx @sentry/mcp-server@latest --host=sentry.example.com"
       - --outputTransport
       - streamableHttp
       - --healthEndpoint
       - "/healthz"
       - --stateful
       - --sessionTimeout
       - "300000"
     environment:
       SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN}
     healthcheck:
       test: ["CMD", "wget", "--spider", "-q", "http://localhost:8000/healthz"]
       interval: 30s
       timeout: 5s
       retries: 3
       start_period: 30s
   ```

1. Set `SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the environment that the Compose file reads.

1. Start the container.

1. In the sidebar, select **Settings** → **Global MCP servers**.

1. Under **Built-in**, select **Edit** on the `sentry` server.

1. Set **URL** to `http://mcp-sentry:8000/mcp`.

1. Under **Headers**, remove the `Authorization` header, because the bridge authenticates with its own `SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

1. Select **Test connection**.

1. Under **Status**, select **Active**.

1. Select **Save**.

Replace `sentry.example.com` with your Sentry host. For a Sentry that serves plain HTTP, add `--insecure-http` to the `npx` command.

### Deploy Sentry's worker

The [sentry-mcp](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-mcp) repository ships the open-source Cloudflare worker behind mcp.sentry.dev. Deploying your own instance gives you an HTTP endpoint without a bridge. Set the `sentry` server's URL to your worker, and keep the `Authorization: Sentry-Bearer <token>` header on it.

## Personal servers

Every member, admins included, can add personal MCP servers from the **MCP Servers** page. **New server** there always creates a server that you own. Personal servers use the same transports, tool filters and **Test connection** as global custom servers, with these differences.

**Where they load.** A personal server loads only in runs where DAIV knows whom the run acts as. Those are chat sessions, dashboard-started runs, jobs submitted through the API or MCP interface, and runs that a GitLab or GitHub event starts for a person who signed in to DAIV with that platform account (an issue label or mention, or a mention on a merge request a DAIV session owns). A session's CI fixes act as its owner, and a resumed delegation as the user who delegated. A mention on a merge request no session owns, or by someone who never signed in with that account, has no acting user, and DAIV loads **global servers only**.

**Header values are always literal.** A personal server's headers cannot be an `env_ref`, so a member cannot probe the DAIV host's environment through their own configuration.

**Name collisions.** A personal server cannot take a global server's name when you create it. If an admin later adds a global server with the same name, the global server wins while it is **Active** or **On-demand**: DAIV skips the personal server in every run, and the **MCP Servers** page flags it with a **Shadowed** badge.

**Admin oversight.** On the **MCP Servers** page, admins have an owner dropdown, set to **You** by default, to list any member's personal servers. Admins can disable, delete or refresh those servers. They cannot edit them or see their header values.

### Resolve a name collision

You cannot rename a server, so you delete the shadowed personal server and create it again under another name.

Deleting a server deletes its headers

DAIV removes the server and its stored headers permanently, and the form never shows header values. Keep the values somewhere else before you delete. A new server starts with no headers.

1. In the sidebar, select **Settings** → **MCP servers**.
1. Find the server marked **Shadowed**, and note its settings. Have its header values from your own records, because the form never shows them.
1. Select **Delete** on it.
1. On the confirmation page, select **Delete**.
1. Select **New server**.
1. Enter a **Name** that no global server uses, then re-enter the other settings and headers (see [Add a server](#add-a-server)).
1. Select **Save**.

## Related pages

- [MCP endpoint](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/mcp-endpoint/index.md): the reverse direction, which exposes DAIV itself as an MCP server so Claude Code, Cursor or Codex CLI can delegate to it.
- [Request Tracker triage](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/integrations/rt/index.md): a worked example of DAIV driven from an external system.
- [Agent tools](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/agent-architecture/index.md): when MCP tools join the agent's tool set.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#mcp-tools): the MCP-related settings.
# Reference

# Environment variables

This page lists the environment variables DAIV reads, with the default and an example for each. Use it to find the variable for a setting, or to check a default you rely on.

In the tables, marks a sensitive variable (an API key, password or token) that you should provide as a Docker secret or from a secure credential manager, and marks a variable you must set.

[Site configuration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/index.md) can change many of these settings at runtime. A variable that has a Site Configuration field overrides the stored value and locks the field; [How environment variables and the UI interact](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#how-environment-variables-and-the-ui-interact) gives the order. Variables marked *env-only* have no field there. The provider API key variables are a different case: DAIV reads them once, as [LLM providers](#llm-providers) explains.

## Core

### Django

| Variable                     | Description                                                        | Default              | Example                 |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `DJANGO_DEBUG`               | Toggle Django debug mode                                           | `False`              | `True`                  |
| `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY`          | Secret key for Django                                              | *(none)*             | `super-secret-key`      |
| `DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`       | Comma-separated list of allowed hosts                              | `*`                  | `example.com,localhost` |
| `DJANGO_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` | Name of the session cookie; give each instance on one host its own | `__Secure-sessionid` | `__Secure-sessionid-1`  |

`DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS` limits the hosts that can reach DAIV. The default `*` allows any host, so list the host DAIV runs on to restrict it.

Warning

Do not turn on `DJANGO_DEBUG` in production. It exposes sensitive information and breaks the security of the application.

Warning

Keep `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` stable and backed up. Unless you set `DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, DAIV derives the key that encrypts stored secrets from it, so a lost or changed `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` makes every stored secret unreadable. See [External URL and encryption key](#external-url-and-encryption-key).

### Uvicorn

| Variable       | Description                     | Default   | Example   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------- | --------- | --------- |
| `UVICORN_HOST` | Host to bind the Uvicorn server | `0.0.0.0` | `0.0.0.0` |
| `UVICORN_PORT` | Port to bind the Uvicorn server | `8000`    | `8000`    |

### Database

| Variable                 | Description                                                                   | Default     | Example      |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------ |
| `DB_NAME`                | Database name                                                                 | *(none)*    | `daiv`       |
| `DB_USER`                | Database user                                                                 | *(none)*    | `daiv_admin` |
| `DB_PASSWORD`            | Database password                                                             | *(none)*    |              |
| `DB_HOST`                | Database host                                                                 | `localhost` | `db`         |
| `DB_PORT`                | Database port                                                                 | `5432`      | `5432`       |
| `DB_SSLMODE`             | PostgreSQL SSL mode                                                           | `require`   | `prefer`     |
| `DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE`       | Maximum size of a connection pool                                             | `15`        | `30`         |
| `DB_KEEPALIVES_IDLE`     | Seconds a pooled connection may sit idle before a TCP keepalive probe is sent | `60`        | `120`        |
| `DB_KEEPALIVES_INTERVAL` | Seconds between TCP keepalive probes on a pooled connection                   | `10`        | `10`         |
| `DB_KEEPALIVES_COUNT`    | Unanswered keepalive probes before a pooled connection is considered dead     | `5`         | `5`          |

### Redis

| Variable                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Default                     | Example                |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `DJANGO_REDIS_URL`                    | Redis connection URL for cache (DB 0)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | *(none)*                    | `redis://redis:6379/0` |
| `DJANGO_REDIS_SESSION_URL`            | Redis connection URL for sessions (DB 1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Value of `DJANGO_REDIS_URL` | `redis://redis:6379/1` |
| `DJANGO_REDIS_CHECKPOINT_URL`         | Redis connection URL for LangGraph checkpoints. Needs Redis 8 or later and database `0`, the only one Redis search can index                                                                                                                                                 | Value of `DJANGO_REDIS_URL` | `redis://redis:6379/0` |
| `DJANGO_REDIS_CHECKPOINT_TTL_MINUTES` | TTL in minutes for LangGraph checkpoint data, the agent's working copy; an expired session resumes from its database archive. Each write expires on its own, so the agent no longer sees the oldest messages of a thread active for longer than this; the archive keeps them | `10080` (7 days)            | `1440`                 |

### Sentry

| Variable                      | Description                                                              | Default  | Example      |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------------ |
| `SENTRY_DSN`                  | Sentry DSN                                                               | *(none)* |              |
| `ENVIRONMENT`                 | Deployment environment name, reported to Sentry as the event environment | *(none)* | `production` |
| `SENTRY_DEBUG`                | Enable Sentry debug mode                                                 | `False`  | `True`       |
| `SENTRY_ENABLE_LOGS`          | Enable Sentry logs                                                       | `False`  | `True`       |
| `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`   | Sentry traces sample rate                                                | `0.0`    | `1.0`        |
| `SENTRY_PROFILES_SAMPLE_RATE` | Sentry profiles sample rate                                              | `0.0`    | `1.0`        |
| `SENTRY_SEND_DEFAULT_PII`     | Enable Sentry default PII                                                | `False`  | `True`       |
| `NODE_HOSTNAME`               | Node hostname, reported to Sentry as the event server name               | *(none)* |              |
| `SERVICE_NAME`                | Service name, reported to Sentry as the `service_name` tag               | *(none)* |              |

### Logging

| Variable               | Description          | Default   | Example |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- | --------- | ------- |
| `DJANGO_LOGGING_LEVEL` | Django logging level | `WARNING` | `DEBUG` |

### Monitoring (LangSmith)

| Variable             | Description              | Default                           | Example                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `LANGSMITH_TRACING`  | Enable LangSmith tracing | `false`                           | `true`                               |
| `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`  | LangSmith project name   | `default`                         | `daiv-production`                    |
| `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`  | LangSmith API key        | *(none)*                          | `lsv2_pt_...`                        |
| `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT` | LangSmith API endpoint   | `https://api.smith.langchain.com` | `https://eu.api.smith.langchain.com` |

The LangSmith variables also accept the `LANGCHAIN_` prefix, for example `LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2` and `LANGCHAIN_API_KEY`. `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` also accepts a Docker secret through the `_FILE` suffix. For setup, see [Monitoring](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/monitoring/index.md).

### Time zone

DAIV runs in the `Europe/Lisbon` time zone. It is fixed in the settings and is not a variable. A time you give without an offset, such as a schedule's run time or the value of `create_api_key --expires-at`, is read in that zone. Add an offset, for example `+00:00`, to give a time in another zone.

### Sandbox (client-side)

| Variable                               | Description                                                                                                                                     | Default               | Example                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_URL`                     | URL of the sandbox service                                                                                                                      | `http://sandbox:8000` | `http://sandbox:8000`       |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT`                 | Timeout for sandbox requests in seconds, and the longest timeout the agent can give a bash command, whose request waits up to 60 seconds longer | `600`                 | `600`                       |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY`                 | API key for sandbox requests                                                                                                                    | *(none)*              | `random-api-key`            |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_DISALLOW` | JSON array of extra bash command rules to block globally                                                                                        | *(none)*              | `'["curl", "npm publish"]'` |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_ALLOW`    | JSON array of bash command rules to permit; has no effect (see [Precedence](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/#precedence))       | *(none)*              | `'["my-safe-tool"]'`        |

Both command policy settings take a JSON array. A plain string such as `curl wget`, or an empty value, fails to parse and DAIV does not start. The outer single quotes in the examples are YAML or shell quoting, not part of the value. For how entries are matched and which rules are built in, see [Sandbox](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/#global-rules).

The sandbox service has its own settings; see [Deployment files](#deployment-files) and the [daiv-sandbox](https://github.com/srtab/daiv-sandbox) repository.

### Authentication

DAIV uses [django-allauth](https://docs.allauth.org/) for web authentication. Users sign in with a Git platform account (GitHub or GitLab) or with a passwordless login code sent by email. Email signup is off. For how accounts are created, see [Accounts and roles](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#sign-in), and for [who becomes the first admin](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#the-first-admin), the section of that page.

The OAuth variables below override the matching fields of the **Authentication** group of Site Configuration and lock them; the group also holds an **Enable OAuth login** toggle. To create the OAuth app that gives you the client ID and secret, see [Create the OAuth app](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#create-the-oauth-app).

| Variable                    | Description                                                                                                                               | Default                                       | Example                                          |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `DAIV_AUTH_LOGIN_ENABLED`   | Show the social provider button on the login page                                                                                         | `false`                                       | `true`                                           |
| `DAIV_AUTH_SIGNUP_OPEN`     | Allow anyone authenticating via the configured Git platform to self-create an account. When off, only admin-pre-created users can sign in | `false`                                       | `true`                                           |
| `ALLAUTH_CLIENT_ID`         | OAuth client ID for the configured Git platform                                                                                           | *(none)*                                      | `Iv1.abc123`                                     |
| `ALLAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`     | OAuth client secret for the configured Git platform                                                                                       | *(none)*                                      |                                                  |
| `ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL`        | GitLab instance URL (for OAuth redirects to the user's browser)                                                                           | `https://gitlab.com`                          | `https://gitlab.example.com`                     |
| `ALLAUTH_GITLAB_SERVER_URL` | GitLab server URL (for server-to-server API calls, if different from `ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL`)                                                | *(none)*                                      | `http://gitlab:8929`                             |
| `EMAIL_BACKEND`             | Django email backend for login-by-code emails                                                                                             | `django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend` | `django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend` |
| `EMAIL_HOST`                | SMTP server hostname                                                                                                                      | `localhost`                                   | `smtp.example.com`                               |
| `EMAIL_PORT`                | SMTP server port                                                                                                                          | `25`                                          | `587`                                            |
| `EMAIL_HOST_USER`           | SMTP authentication username                                                                                                              | *(empty)*                                     | `user@example.com`                               |
| `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD`       | SMTP authentication password                                                                                                              | *(empty)*                                     |                                                  |
| `EMAIL_USE_TLS`             | Use TLS for SMTP connection                                                                                                               | `False`                                       | `True`                                           |
| `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`        | Sender address for login-by-code emails                                                                                                   | `noreply@daiv.dev`                            | `noreply@example.com`                            |

OAuth login needs all three of the `DAIV_AUTH_LOGIN_ENABLED` toggle, a client ID and a client secret. If you set only one of the client ID and the secret, DAIV logs a warning and does not show the provider button on the login page. The `CODEBASE_CLIENT` setting decides which provider, GitHub or GitLab, DAIV offers.

With `EMAIL_BACKEND` set to `django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend`, DAIV writes login-code emails to the app's output instead of sending them, which is enough to sign in without an SMTP server.

### Rocket.Chat

Enabling the **Rocket Chat** group offers Rocket.Chat as a notification channel that users can opt into.

| Variable                     | Description                                                  | Default  | Example                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `DAIV_ROCKETCHAT_ENABLED`    | Offer Rocket.Chat as a notification channel for users        | `false`  | `true`                   |
| `DAIV_ROCKETCHAT_URL`        | Base URL of your Rocket.Chat instance                        | *(none)* | `https://rc.example.com` |
| `DAIV_ROCKETCHAT_USER_ID`    | The bot user's `_id`, sent as the `X-User-Id` header         | *(none)* | `abc123userid`           |
| `DAIV_ROCKETCHAT_AUTH_TOKEN` | The bot user's auth token, sent as the `X-Auth-Token` header | *(none)* |                          |

### Telegram

Enabling Telegram offers it as a notification channel that users can opt into. DAIV derives the bot username and generates the webhook secret itself; see [Telegram derived values](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#telegram-derived-values).

| Variable                  | Description                                                  | Default  | Example |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------- |
| `DAIV_TELEGRAM_ENABLED`   | Offer Telegram as a notification channel for users           | `false`  | `true`  |
| `DAIV_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot token issued by @BotFather, in the form `123456:ABC-DEF` | *(none)* |         |

Two more variables exist, but leave them unset: each pins a value that DAIV otherwise derives.

| Variable                       | Description                                                                                                    | Default       | Example    |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------- |
| `DAIV_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME`   | Pins the bot username. A value that disagrees with the token breaks the connect link, and nothing corrects it. | *(derived)*   | `daiv_bot` |
| `DAIV_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Pins the webhook secret. It must not be empty: a blank value makes the webhook reject every update.            | *(generated)* |            |

### External URL and encryption key

| Variable              | Description                                                                                                               | Default                  | Example                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`   | External URL of the application.                                                                                          | `https://127.0.0.1:8000` | `https://daiv.example.com` |
| `DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Fernet encryption key for secrets stored in the database. If not set, a key is derived from `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` via HKDF. | *(derived)*              |                            |

DAIV uses `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` to define webhooks on the Git platform and as the site domain in authentication emails, so the Git platform must be able to reach it.

`DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY` protects the secrets DAIV stores in its database: provider API keys, the Tavily web search API key, the OAuth client secret, the sandbox API key, the Rocket.Chat token, the Telegram bot token and webhook secret, web fetch header values, MCP server headers, and sandbox environment variables and egress secrets. DAIV uses a raw Fernet key directly. Any other value is a passphrase, from which DAIV derives a key with HKDF-SHA256. When the variable is unset, DAIV derives the key from `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY`.

Warning

Back up `DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, or `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` when you leave it unset. If the key is lost or changed, DAIV cannot decrypt the stored secrets, and you must enter them again.

### Analytics

| Variable                | Description                                                                                                                              | Default                            | Example                                |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` | [Umami](https://umami.is/) website ID. When set, the public homepage and `/compare/` pages load Umami's tracker for signed-out visitors. | *(none)*                           | `0b6bd0c4-5d6c-4f2e-9a43-1d2e3f4a5b6c` |
| `DAIV_UMAMI_SCRIPT_URL` | URL of Umami's tracker script; set it to use a self-hosted Umami.                                                                        | `https://cloud.umami.is/script.js` | `https://stats.example.com/script.js`  |

Analytics is off unless you set `DAIV_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID`, so DAIV sends no visitor data by default. When it is set, the tracker uses no cookies, honours the browser's Do Not Track setting, and never loads for signed-in users or on dashboard pages.
