## Codebase

### Git platform

| Variable                              | Description                                                                                                      | Default        | Example              |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------- |
| `CODEBASE_CLIENT`                     | Client to use for codebase operations                                                                            | `gitlab`       | `gitlab` or `github` |
| `CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON`         | Cron expression for periodic webhook setup (GitLab only)                                                         | `*/5 * * * *`  | `*/10 * * * *`       |
| `CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_SYNC_CRON`      | Cron expression for the periodic repository access sync                                                          | `*/15 * * * *` | `*/10 * * * *`       |
| `CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_HARD_TTL_HOURS` | Hours a repository's synced access data stays trusted before it is denied (fails closed); tracked per repository | `24`           | `12`                 |

Set `CODEBASE_CLIENT` to `gitlab` or `github`. Only one platform is active at a time.

`CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_SYNC_CRON` sets how often DAIV copies each user's repository membership from the Git platform into its database, with one member-list call per repository. Admins are exempt from repository authorization and always have full access. DAIV tracks freshness per repository: if a repository's sync stops succeeding, for example because the platform token loses access to it, DAIV keeps using the last known access data until `CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_HARD_TTL_HOURS` elapse. After that the repository denies access, while the others keep syncing. See [Accounts and roles](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#repository-access) for the access model.

### GitLab

| Variable                         | Description                                                                                               | Default  | Example                 |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL`            | URL of the GitLab instance                                                                                | *(none)* | `https://gitlab.com`    |
| `CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN`     | Authentication token for GitLab                                                                           | *(none)* | `glpat-xyz`             |
| `CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secret token for GitLab webhook validation. Without it, every GitLab webhook request is rejected with 401 | *(none)* | `random-webhook-secret` |

`CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN` is a personal access token with the `api` scope.

For `git clone` and `git push`, DAIV does not put this token in the repository workspace. It creates a short-lived project access token for each repository instead: named `daiv-clone`, with the `write_repository` scope and the Developer access level, and valid for 48 to 72 hours. DAIV reuses a repository's token for up to 24 hours, so expect a few `daiv-clone` bot members on a project at a time. GitLab removes expired ones.

Creating these tokens needs the token's user to hold at least the Maintainer role on each project and, on GitLab.com, the Premium or Ultimate tier. Self-managed instances accept any tier. When DAIV cannot create a token, it logs a warning and falls back to the personal access token.

The project access token pushes at the Developer level. If a branch protection rule matches the branches DAIV pushes to, for example a wildcard pattern that limits pushes to Maintainers, allow Developers to push on that pattern, or pushes fail.

Warning

Revoking a `daiv-clone` token early makes the next clone of that project fail authentication until DAIV drops the cached token and creates a new one, which happens after about 15 seconds of retries. The cache entry is `codebase:gitlab:clone-token:<project-id>`.

### GitHub

| Variable                          | Description                                                                                               | Default  | Example                 |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL`             | URL of the GitHub instance                                                                                | *(none)* | `https://github.com`    |
| `CODEBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID`          | GitHub App ID                                                                                             | *(none)* | `123456`                |
| `CODEBASE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID` | GitHub App Installation ID                                                                                | *(none)* | `789012`                |
| `CODEBASE_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY`     | GitHub App private key (PEM format)                                                                       | *(none)* |                         |
| `CODEBASE_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`  | Secret token for GitHub webhook validation. Without it, every GitHub webhook request is rejected with 401 | *(none)* | `random-webhook-secret` |

GitHub uses GitHub App authentication, so you create a GitHub App in your account or organization settings. The private key is a multi-line PEM file; store it as a Docker secret. For GitHub Enterprise Server, set `CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL` to its URL, for example `https://github.example.com`. For GitHub.com, you can omit it.

______________________________________________________________________

## LLM providers

Configure at least one provider to use the agent. The [LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md) page explains how model specs pick a provider.

Provider keys are seed-only

DAIV reads the provider API key variables once, when it first creates the provider records, and never again. They are not part of the environment, database and default order that other settings follow. Changing or adding a `*_API_KEY` variable or secret after the provider record exists has no effect: edit the provider under **Configuration** → **Providers** instead, which holds the key and the base URL from then on. A provider created without a key starts disabled.

DAIV reads each key from a Docker secret named after the variable in lowercase, for example `openrouter_api_key` mounted at `/run/secrets/openrouter_api_key`, or else from the environment variable. The secret wins when both are set. The OpenRouter base URL is a **Base URL** field of the provider and defaults to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. [Providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#providers) describes the fields.

### OpenRouter (default)

| Variable             | Description                                                            | Default  | Example |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key (seeds the OpenRouter provider record on first run) | *(none)* |         |

### Anthropic

| Variable            | Description                                                          | Default  | Example |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key (seeds the Anthropic provider record on first run) | *(none)* |         |

### OpenAI

| Variable         | Description                                                    | Default  | Example |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key (seeds the OpenAI provider record on first run) | *(none)* |         |

### Google

| Variable         | Description                                                    | Default  | Example |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Google API key (seeds the Google provider record on first run) | *(none)* |         |

## Agent tools

These variables configure the tools the agent calls.

### Context file suggestion

| Variable                            | Description                                                         | Default | Example |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `DAIV_SUGGEST_CONTEXT_FILE_ENABLED` | Enable/disable suggesting an `AGENTS.md` file on new merge requests | `true`  | `false` |

### Web search

| Variable                                  | Description                                                                     | Default      | Example                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED`                 | Enable/disable the `web_search` tool                                            | `true`       | `false`                             |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS`             | Maximum number of results to return from web search                             | `5`          |                                     |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE`                  | Web search engine to use (`duckduckgo`, `tavily`, `searxng`)                    | `duckduckgo` | `searxng`                           |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY`                 | Web search API key (required if engine is `tavily`)                             | *(none)*     |                                     |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_URL`             | Complete SearXNG search endpoint, including `/search` and any deployment prefix | *(none)*     | `https://search.example.com/search` |
| `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | SearXNG HTTP timeout in seconds (1–120); does not change other engines          | `15`         | `30`                                |

To use SearXNG, see [Set up SearXNG](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/site-configuration/#set-up-searxng).

### Web fetch

The native `web_fetch` tool fetches a URL, converts HTML to markdown, and has a small model answer a prompt about the page. A `#fragment` on an HTML page's URL limits it to the section that anchor names. A page over the maximum content size is rejected with a list of its section anchors.

| Variable                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                     | Default                                 | Example                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_ENABLED`           | Enable/disable the native `web_fetch` tool                                                                                                                                      | `true`                                  | `false`                                    |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_MODEL_NAME`        | Model used by `web_fetch` to process page content with the prompt                                                                                                               | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | `openrouter:openai/gpt-4.1-mini`           |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | Cache TTL (seconds) for repeated fetches                                                                                                                                        | `900`                                   | `1800`                                     |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`   | HTTP timeout for fetching (seconds)                                                                                                                                             | `15`                                    | `30`                                       |
| `AUTOMATION_WEB_FETCH_PROXY_URL`   | Optional proxy URL for web fetch HTTP requests (env-only)                                                                                                                       | *(none)*                                | `http://proxy:8080`                        |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS` | Max page content size (characters) to analyze in one pass                                                                                                                       | `50000`                                 | `80000`                                    |
| `DAIV_WEB_FETCH_AUTH_HEADERS`      | Domain-to-headers mapping for authenticated fetches (JSON). When set, it replaces the **Per-domain auth headers** rows of the **Web Fetch** group, which then show a lock badge | `{}`                                    | `{"example.com": {"X-API-Key": "sk-abc"}}` |

### Artifacts

The `publish_artifact` tool stores files the agent generates (reports, datasets, charts) as run [artifacts](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/#artifacts), served from the dashboard. Files are written to Django's default file storage (`MEDIA_ROOT`, `~/data/media` in the containers), which the web and worker containers must share.

| Variable                      | Description                                                                               | Default             | Example    |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------- |
| `DAIV_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES`     | Maximum size of one published file, in bytes (at most 64 MiB, the sandbox download limit) | `10485760` (10 MiB) | `52428800` |
| `DAIV_ARTIFACTS_PER_RUN_MAX`  | Maximum number of files one run may publish                                               | `20`                | `50`       |
| `DAIV_TOOL_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES`   | Maximum size of one image or file kept from a tool result for the transcript, in bytes    | `10485760` (10 MiB) | `20971520` |
| `DAIV_TOOL_MEDIA_PER_RUN_MAX` | Maximum number of images and files kept from one run's tool results                       | `100`               | `200`      |

### Session transcript

| Variable                  | Description                                                                                                                           | Default                    | Example |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------- |
| `DAIV_SHOW_RAW_TOOL_DATA` | Show each tool call's raw arguments and result in a closed **Raw** section of the call's details in the session transcript (env-only) | *(follows `DJANGO_DEBUG`)* | `true`  |

### MCP tools

MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools give the agent access to external services. DAIV stores MCP servers as database rows, which you manage at `/dashboard/mcp-servers/`, and connects to them directly, with no sidecar containers. For user-defined servers, see [MCP tools](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/mcp-tools/index.md).

| Variable                | Description                                                                                                                                  | Default | Example |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `MCP_TOOL_LOAD_TIMEOUT` | Max seconds to wait for a single MCP server to return its tools before skipping it (keeps a broken/slow server from freezing chats and runs) | `30`    | `10`    |

### Deferred tools

With deferred tools on, DAIV loads tools outside the always-loaded set on demand through a `tool_search` tool, instead of binding them to the model up front. Most deployments do not need to change these variables.

| Variable                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Default                                                                                 | Example         |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_ENABLED`                  | Defer non-essential tools behind `tool_search` instead of binding them eagerly                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `true`                                                                                  | `false`         |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_TOP_K_DEFAULT`            | Default number of results returned by a `tool_search` call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `3`                                                                                     | `5`             |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_TOP_K_MAX`                | Maximum number of results `tool_search` will return per call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `10`                                                                                    | `20`            |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_FROZEN_TOOLS_MODELS`      | Prefix-matched model names whose bound tools array is kept frozen (loaded schemas reach them via `tool_search` results only), preserving the provider prompt cache. Empty list disables freezing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `claude-,anthropic/claude-,qwen/qwen3.8-max,minimax/minimax-m3,google/gemini-3.7-flash` | `claude-`       |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_INLINE_TOOLS_MODELS`      | Prefix-matched model names that get each loaded tool declared mid-conversation, right after the `tool_search` result that loaded it, through the provider's native mechanism (Anthropic `tool_addition`, OpenAI Responses `additional_tools`). The tools array stays frozen, so loading a tool keeps the prompt cache, and the model calls a declared tool. Applies only to models reached through the Anthropic API, or through an OpenAI-typed provider over the Responses API (the provider's Responses API setting is on, or the model is GPT 6, which langchain-openai sends there whenever tools are bound); on the Anthropic API, only to models langchain-anthropic keeps mid-conversation system messages in place for (not Claude Sonnet 5 or Haiku 5.5, for example). Empty list disables it. | `claude-,gpt-6-sol,gpt-6-luna,gpt-5.6-luna`                                             | `claude-opus-5` |
| `DEFERRED_TOOLS_EMBED_SCHEMAS_IN_RESULTS` | Embed each loaded tool's full schema in the `tool_search` result. Emergency valve: when `false`, results carry summaries only **and freezing and inline definitions are forced off**, so every model falls back to the array-append + summary pre-change behaviour.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `true`                                                                                  | `false`         |

## Agents

These variables set the models and behavior of DAIV's agents. A repository can override the models in `.daiv.yml`; see [Model overrides](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/#model-overrides).

### DAIV agent

The main agent handles issue addressing, pull request assistance and all interactive tasks. Its variables use the `DAIV_AGENT_` prefix.

| Variable                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Default                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT`         | Maximum recursion depth for agent execution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `500`                                    |
| `DAIV_AGENT_MODEL_NAME`              | Primary model for agent tasks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| `DAIV_AGENT_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME`     | Fallback model if the primary model fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `openrouter:openai/gpt-6.1-sol`          |
| `DAIV_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL`          | Extended thinking level (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, in any case; empty or `off` to disable)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `medium`                                 |
| `DAIV_AGENT_FALLBACK_THINKING_LEVEL` | Thinking level applied when the primary model fails over to the fallback model (same values as `DAIV_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL`, set independently of it)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `medium`                                 |
| `DAIV_AGENT_MAX_MODEL_NAME`          | Model used when the `daiv-max` label is present                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`   |
| `DAIV_AGENT_MAX_THINKING_LEVEL`      | Thinking level for `daiv-max` tasks (same values as `DAIV_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `high`                                   |
| `DAIV_AGENT_SKILL_MODELS`            | Model per skill name, as a JSON object (`{"code-review": "openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5"}`); see [Agent skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/#run-a-skill-on-another-model). A null or empty entry is unset; a malformed value is logged and ignored.                                                                                                           | `{}`                                     |
| `DAIV_AGENT_SUBAGENT_MODELS`         | Model per subagent name, as a JSON object (`{"explore": "openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5"}`). See [Subagents](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/#subagent-model-precedence). A null or empty entry is unset; a malformed value is logged and ignored. The deprecated `DAIV_AGENT_EXPLORE_MODEL_NAME` is read as the `explore` entry when there is none, and DAIV logs an error. | `{}`                                     |
| `DAIV_AGENT_CUSTOM_SKILLS_PATH`      | Path to custom global skills directory. Set to `None` to disable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `~/data/skills`                          |
| `DAIV_SESSION_LINK_ENABLED`          | Link back to the DAIV sessions that produced the changes, from the descriptions of merge requests DAIV opens and from a DAIV-Session trailer on every commit. Disable to keep the DAIV URL off the git platform                                                                                                                                                                                       | `true`                                   |

### Model requests

These bound every LLM API call, whatever the provider: the main agent, subagents, and the model-backed tasks (titling, memory, commit/PR writer, web fetch). Without them a stalled provider can block a run indefinitely.

| Variable                             | Description                                                                          | Default |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `DAIV_MODEL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-request timeout for LLM API calls, in seconds. Minimum `1`.                      | `120`   |
| `DAIV_MODEL_MAX_RETRIES`             | Retries for a failed LLM API call before the error propagates (`0` disables retries) | `2`     |

### Jobs API

The [Jobs API](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/jobs-api/index.md) runs the agent from your own code.

| Variable                  | Description                                                                                                                                             | Default   |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `DAIV_JOBS_THROTTLE_RATE` | Rate limit for job submissions per authenticated user. Format: `N/sec`, `N/min`, `N/hour`, or `N/day`, or the short forms `N/s`, `N/m`, `N/h` and `N/d` | `20/hour` |

### Diff to metadata

Generates pull request titles, descriptions and commit messages from diffs.

| Variable                                    | Description                                   | Default                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_DIFF_TO_METADATA_MODEL_NAME`          | Primary model for diff-to-metadata generation | `openrouter:google/gemini-3.8-flash`      |
| `DAIV_DIFF_TO_METADATA_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME` | Fallback model if the primary model fails     | `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` |

### Titling

Generates short titles for sessions and runs from the user's initial prompt.

| Variable                           | Description                               | Default                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_TITLING_MODEL_NAME`          | Primary model for title generation        | `openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna`          |
| `DAIV_TITLING_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME` | Fallback model if the primary model fails | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` |

### Memory

Learns from finished runs, consolidates what they teach into a per-repository document, and injects it into future runs.

| Variable                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                            | Default                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_ENABLED`                            | Capture learnings from finished runs, consolidate them, and inject them into future runs. A per-repository `.daiv.yml` flag can still opt an individual repository out | `true`                                  |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_MODEL_NAME`              | Cheap model that extracts candidate observations from each finished run's transcript                                                                                   | `openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna`          |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME`     | Fallback model when the extraction model fails                                                                                                                         | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL_NAME`           | Model that rewrites the memory document. Leave empty to reuse the repository's agent model                                                                             | *(none)*                                |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MIN_PENDING`          | Consolidate once at least this many pending observations have accumulated (subject to the consolidation interval below)                                                | `10`                                    |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_PENDING_AGE_DAYS` | Consolidate a repository that is still below the threshold above once its oldest pending observation reaches this age, so low-volume repositories still form memory    | `7`                                     |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS`   | Minimum hours between consolidations for the same repository                                                                                                           | `24`                                    |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_MAX_LINES`                          | Cap on the memory document length in lines; entries beyond it are evicted                                                                                              | `200`                                   |
| `DAIV_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES`                          | Cap on the memory document size in bytes; entries beyond it are evicted                                                                                                | `10240`                                 |

### Run classifier

Classifies the report of each finished scheduled run into an envelope.

| Variable                                  | Description                                                                 | Default                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `DAIV_RUN_CLASSIFIER_MODEL_NAME`          | Model that classifies each finished scheduled run's report into an envelope | `openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna`          |
| `DAIV_RUN_CLASSIFIER_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME` | Fallback model when the classifier model fails                              | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` |

### Pipeline watch

Watches the CI of merge requests DAIV publishes and spends a bounded number of agent runs fixing failures; see [Pipeline watch](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/pipeline-watch/index.md).

| Variable                           | Description                                                                          | Default |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `DAIV_PIPELINE_WATCH_ENABLED`      | Watch CI on merge requests DAIV publishes and try to fix failures                    | `true`  |
| `DAIV_PIPELINE_WATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | How many fix attempts to spend on one merge request before handing back (at least 1) | `3`     |

______________________________________________________________________

## Deployment files

The sample deployment files set the variables below. The `DAIV_SANDBOX_*` variables configure the [daiv-sandbox](https://github.com/srtab/daiv-sandbox) container, not the DAIV app, and Docker reads `DAIV_IMAGE_TAG` when it starts the stack.

| Variable                           | Read by         | Description                                                                                                                                                | Default  | Example                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_REDIS_URL`           | Sandbox service | Redis URL for per-session locking and for removing running sessions that stop receiving requests. Without it, the sandbox disables both and logs a warning | *(none)* | `redis://redis:6379/3`                     |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_CERT_FILE` | Sandbox service | Path to the egress CA certificate that the sandbox's egress proxy signs with. Set it together with the key file: the sandbox does not start with only one  | *(none)* | `/run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert` |
| `DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_KEY_FILE`  | Sandbox service | Path to the egress CA private key. Without both files, the sandbox rejects sessions that need the egress proxy and the run fails                           | *(none)* | `/run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key`  |
| `DAIV_IMAGE_TAG`                   | Docker          | Tag of the DAIV image that the sample services pull; pin it to roll back to a build                                                                        | `main`   | `sha-5e4f0d0`                              |

To create the egress CA and store it as secrets, see [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md).

# Site configuration

Site Configuration is the admin-only page where you change DAIV's runtime behavior without redeploying. It groups settings by area and stores them in the database. You pick agent models, turn agent tools on or off, register LLM providers and switch OAuth login on or off, unless an environment variable or Docker secret overrides the field.

## Open the configuration page

You need an account with the **admin** role. Members do not see Site Configuration, and a member who opens its address is denied access.

1. Sign in as an admin.
1. Open `/dashboard/configuration/`. DAIV redirects you to the first group, **Agent**, at `/dashboard/configuration/agent/`.
1. Select a group. Each group is a page at `/dashboard/configuration/<group_key>/`, and an unknown key returns a 404.
1. Change the fields, then select **Save configuration**. DAIV shows "Configuration saved."

Saving a group writes only that group's fields. A saved change takes effect immediately for the next read: the save commits in a transaction and clears the read cache when it commits. An agent run reads its settings once, when it starts, so a change applies from the next run. The read cache keeps a value for 5 minutes, which matters only for changes made outside this page, such as a direct database edit: they can take that long to appear.

## Setting groups

The configuration has the following groups, organized by category.

| Group                  | Category     | What it configures                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Agent**              | AI tasks     | Primary, fallback and `daiv-max` models; their thinking levels; the agent recursion limit; the per-request LLM timeout and retry count (applied to every provider and model-backed task); whether to suggest a context file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`) on new merge requests; whether to link sessions from merge requests; and **Subagent models**, the model the general-purpose and explore subagents run on in every repository (see [Subagents](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/#subagent-model-precedence)). An entry already stored for a skill or subagent that only repositories define is listed there too, so it can be changed or cleared. A skill's model, and those of the code-review detectors, are set on the skill's page in **Skills** (see [Agent skills](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/#run-a-skill-on-another-model)). |
| **Commit & PR Writer** | AI tasks     | Primary and fallback models that generate commit messages and pull/merge request descriptions from diffs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Titling**            | AI tasks     | Primary and fallback models that generate session and run titles from prompts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Memory**             | AI tasks     | Capture learnings from finished runs, consolidate them into a per-repository memory document, and inject them into future runs. The models that extract observations from each finished run's transcript and rewrite the memory document, the consolidation thresholds (minimum pending observations, maximum pending age, minimum interval), and the caps on the memory document's lines and bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Run classifier**     | AI tasks     | Primary and fallback models that classify each finished scheduled run's report into an envelope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Providers**          | Models       | LLM provider records (slug, wire protocol, base URL, API key, extra headers and more) that every model field draws from. See [Providers](#providers).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Web Search**         | Agent tools  | Turn the web search tool on or off, pick DuckDuckGo, Tavily or SearXNG, set the maximum results, store the Tavily API key, and set the SearXNG search URL and timeout. See [Set up SearXNG](#set-up-searxng).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Web Fetch**          | Agent tools  | Turn the web fetch tool on or off, choose the model that processes fetched pages, set the cache TTL, timeout and maximum content size, and define per-domain auth headers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Sandbox**            | Runtime      | Sandbox request timeout and the sandbox API key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Jobs**               | Runtime      | Per-user rate limit for [Jobs API](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/jobs-api/index.md) submissions (e.g. `20/hour`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Pipeline Watch**     | Runtime      | Watch CI on merge requests DAIV publishes and try to fix failures, and how many fix attempts (at least 1) to spend on one merge request before handing back.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Rocket Chat**        | Integrations | Offer Rocket.Chat as a notification channel, with the instance URL, bot user ID and auth token.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Telegram**           | Integrations | Offer Telegram as a notification channel, with the bot token from @BotFather. See [Set up Telegram](#set-up-telegram).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Authentication**     | Integrations | OAuth login with your Git platform: the login toggle, open signup, the OAuth client ID and secret and, for GitLab, the instance URLs. See [Turn on OAuth login](#turn-on-oauth-login).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## How environment variables and the UI interact

Each configurable field resolves through three tiers, highest first:

1. **Environment variable or Docker secret.** When set, the matching field is **locked**: the page shows a "Locked by environment variable" tooltip and you cannot edit the field.
1. **Database value.** The value you save here, when it is not empty.
1. **Built-in default.** The value DAIV ships with.

A value you save here takes effect only if no environment variable overrides it. If you leave a field blank, DAIV falls back to the environment variable, if any, and then to the built-in default. To keep a field editable, leave its variable unset rather than set to an empty value: an empty variable still locks the field.

The environment variable for a field is `DAIV_<FIELD_NAME>`; for example, `agent_recursion_limit` maps to `DAIV_AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT`. The **Authentication** fields are the exception and map to the `ALLAUTH_*` variables:

| Field              | Environment variable        |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| OAuth client ID    | `ALLAUTH_CLIENT_ID`         |
| Auth Client Secret | `ALLAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`     |
| GitLab URL         | `ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL`        |
| GitLab server URL  | `ALLAUTH_GITLAB_SERVER_URL` |

[Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/index.md) lists every variable with its default, and marks the ones that are env-only.

## Secrets

DAIV stores the secret fields on this page encrypted in the database: the **Web Search API key**, **Sandbox API key**, **Auth Client Secret**, **Rocketchat Auth Token**, **Telegram Bot Token**, each provider's **API key** and the per-domain web fetch header values. [External URL and encryption key](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#external-url-and-encryption-key) lists everything DAIV encrypts. The page never shows a stored secret again: it shows a masked hint. Leave a secret field blank to keep the stored value, or select **Clear** to remove it. The key comes from `DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

## Providers

The **Providers** group holds the LLM providers DAIV can call. Every model field in the other groups draws its models from the providers you enable here, and a model is written as `<slug>:<model-name>`; [LLM providers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/llm-providers/index.md) explains how a model spec picks its provider.

DAIV creates four built-in providers the first time it runs: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google_genai` and `openrouter`, listed under **Built-in**. Their slug and provider type are locked, and you cannot delete them, but you can set their API keys and base URLs and turn them on or off. A built-in provider whose key was not seeded starts disabled; see [the LLM provider variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#llm-providers) for how the keys are seeded. You add any other provider under **Custom**, for example a vLLM, llama.cpp or LiteLLM server or an internal gateway.

### Provider fields

| Field                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Slug**                    | The prefix of `<slug>:<model-name>`. It starts with a lowercase letter, holds lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and has at most 32 characters. `google` is reserved. It cannot change after creation: delete the provider and add it again to change it. |
| **Display name**            | The name shown in the list. It has at most 64 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Provider type**           | The wire protocol: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenRouter.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Base URL**                | The endpoint to call instead of the provider's default, with an `http` or `https` scheme. For an OpenAI-typed server, include the version segment, for example `/v1`: DAIV warns when it is missing, because requests would reach the wrong route.             |
| **API key**                 | The credential for the endpoint, stored encrypted.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Extra headers (JSON)**    | A JSON object of additional request headers, for example `{"X-Foo": "bar"}`. Header values must be strings. Headers the agent manages itself take precedence.                                                                                                  |
| **Enabled**                 | Whether models can use the provider. Enabling a provider needs an API key.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Use Responses API**       | Applies to OpenAI-typed providers only. Turn it on for servers that expose `/v1/responses`, and leave it off for servers that offer only `/v1/chat/completions`, such as most vLLM, llama.cpp and LiteLLM setups.                                              |
| **Verify TLS certificates** | On by default. Applies to OpenAI- and OpenRouter-typed providers only: for the others, DAIV warns that turning it off has no effect.                                                                                                                           |

A model field anywhere in the configuration is rejected on save when its provider is disabled or has no API key, with a message that points you to the **Providers** group.

### Add a custom provider

Add a provider to use models from a server other than the four built-in providers. You need the admin role, the endpoint's URL and its API key.

1. In **Configuration** → **Providers**, select **Add custom provider**.
1. In **Slug**, enter the model prefix.
1. In **Display name**, enter the name to show in the list.
1. In **Provider type**, choose the wire protocol the server speaks.
1. In **Base URL**, enter the endpoint's URL.
1. In **API key**, enter the key.
1. Select **Save configuration**.
1. Use `<slug>:<model-name>` wherever a model is specified, with `<slug>` replaced by the slug and `<model-name>` by a model the endpoint serves.

Warning

Turn off **Verify TLS certificates** only for self-hosted endpoints behind an internal or self-signed CA. Without verification, the connection is open to man-in-the-middle attacks. Mount the CA certificate into the DAIV containers instead when you can.

## Set up SearXNG

Warning

SearXNG forwards queries to its upstream search engines. Self-hosting does not keep the query text local, and a query can contain repository code or other private information.

By default, web search uses DuckDuckGo. To send the agent's searches to a SearXNG instance instead, you need:

- A SearXNG instance that the DAIV app and workers can reach without authentication, and that allows JSON responses: `json` is in `search.formats` of its settings, for example `[html, json]`.
- The complete search endpoint, for example `https://search.example.com/search`, or `https://search.example.com/searxng/search` when SearXNG runs under a prefix. It must use `http` or `https` and hold no credentials, query string or fragment.
- In **Configuration** → **Web Search**, set **Web search engine** to **SearXNG**.
- Enter the endpoint in **SearXNG search URL**.
- Optionally, set **SearXNG request timeout**, from 1 to 120 seconds. The default is 15 seconds.
- Select **Save configuration**.

Leave the Tavily API key as it is: SearXNG does not use it. The existing maximum results and web search switch apply to SearXNG too. To configure it from the environment instead, set `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE`, `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_URL` and `DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; see [Web search](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#web-search).

DAIV sends a `GET` request with `q` and `format=json` and does not follow redirects, so enter the final endpoint. Chat, GitLab and GitHub runs and other agent entry points share the web search tool, and the model decides when to call it. DAIV itself makes the request, so it does not need an opening in a sandbox environment's egress policy. DAIV keeps HTTPS certificate verification on. A failed search reaches the agent as a tool failure, not as an empty result.

### Allow DAIV through the SearXNG limiter

DAIV sends `Accept-Language: en`, which SearXNG's header checks expect. If the SearXNG limiter (`server.limiter`) is on, it can still answer automated requests with HTTP 429. To exempt DAIV, add its source address to `/etc/searxng/limiter.toml`:

```
[botdetection.ip_lists]
pass_ip = ["192.0.2.10"]
```

Replace `192.0.2.10` with the address SearXNG sees for the DAIV app and workers, or with a narrow trusted subnet. The list exempts those clients from bot detection, so keep it narrow rather than turning the limiter off. For pass lists and reverse-proxy client addresses, see the [SearXNG limiter documentation](https://docs.searxng.org/admin/searx.limiter). For the JSON format setting and the endpoint contract, see the [SearXNG Search API](https://docs.searxng.org/dev/search_api.html).

## Turn on OAuth login

OAuth login lets users sign in with their Git platform account. You need an OAuth app on that platform: see [Create the OAuth app](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/accounts/#create-the-oauth-app).

1. In **Configuration**, open **Authentication**.
1. Turn on the toggle next to the group title. It is the **Enable OAuth login** setting, and DAIV hides the group's other fields while it is off.
1. Enter the **OAuth client ID** and the **Auth Client Secret**. Enter both: DAIV rejects a save that sets only one.
1. On GitLab, set **GitLab URL** to the address your users' browsers open. If DAIV reaches GitLab at a different address, such as one inside a Docker network, set **GitLab server URL** to it. GitHub installs do not show these two fields.
1. Optionally, turn on **Open social signup** to let anyone who authenticates through the Git platform create an account. When it is off, only users an admin created can sign in.
1. Select **Save configuration**.

The `CODEBASE_CLIENT` setting decides which fields the group shows and which provider DAIV offers. DAIV creates no accounts through standard email signup, which is off.

## Set up Telegram

You need a bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/botfather), and a `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` that Telegram can reach.

Warning

Give each DAIV instance its own bot. Telegram allows one webhook per bot, so if a second instance uses the same token, the webhook moves to it and the first instance stops receiving Telegram's updates, including the connect handshake. DAIV's reconcile job logs the URL it finds but cannot prevent this.

1. In **Configuration** → **Telegram**, turn on the toggle next to the group title. It is the **Enable Telegram** setting, and DAIV hides the group's other fields while it is off.
1. Enter the token in **Telegram Bot Token**.
1. Select **Save configuration**.

DAIV checks a typed token with Telegram when you save. It rejects a token Telegram refuses, and saves a token it could not check because Telegram was unreachable, with a warning, so an outage does not block an unrelated edit. The group then shows the bot username. Users connect their account from the notification channels page; see [Notifications](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/notifications/index.md).

## Telegram derived values

You type only the bot token. DAIV derives the rest:

- **Bot username.** DAIV reads it from Telegram with `getMe` when you save the group, and again in a reconcile job that runs every 15 minutes. The page shows it read-only, because a hand-typed username that disagrees with the token breaks the connect link without any visible error. An empty value means the derivation has not run yet.
- **Webhook secret.** DAIV generates it, stores it encrypted and sends it to Telegram when it registers the webhook. You never see it or type it. The webhook rejects every update until the secret exists, so a blank value means the sync has not finished.

Saving is not the only trigger: the reconcile job compares the webhook Telegram has registered with the desired URL and registers it again when they differ. That brings an instance configured only through `DAIV_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `DAIV_TELEGRAM_ENABLED`, which may never open this page, into line, and it recovers a webhook that Telegram disabled after repeated failures.

Turning Telegram off keeps the stored webhook secret. If you turn it off with no bot token available, because you cleared it or never set it while a webhook was registered, DAIV cannot remove the webhook and shows a warning: remove it in BotFather, or restore the token and turn the channel off again. A group that never had a webhook registered saves without a warning.
