# Agent tools

DAIV's agent works through tools: it reads and edits files, runs commands, searches the web and reports back on your git platform. This page lists each tool, when the agent has it, and which settings turn it on or off. The agent is built on [Deep Agents](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents) and runs on [LangGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/).

## Tools bound up front

DAIV binds these tools to the model at the start of every run.

| Tool                              | What it does                                                                                                                                      | When the agent has it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ls`, `read_file`, `glob`, `grep` | List directories, read files, find files by pattern and search file contents by regular expression                                                | Always                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `write_file`, `edit_file`         | Create a file, or change an existing one                                                                                                          | Always                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `bash`                            | Run a command in the persistent, isolated [sandbox](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/index.md), after the command policy checks it | When the run has a sandbox. [How an environment is resolved](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox-environments/#how-an-environment-is-resolved) says when it has one.                                                                                                                           |
| `write_todos`                     | Track the steps of a task                                                                                                                         | Always                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `skill`                           | Run a [skill](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/agent-skills/index.md)                                                                 | Always                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `task`                            | Hand work to a [subagent](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/index.md)                                                             | Always                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ask_user_question`               | Ask you 1 to 4 questions and end the turn, and your answer arrives as the next message                                                            | On the main agent only, and not on a run nobody can answer: a scheduled run, a [pipeline watch](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/pipeline-watch/index.md) run or a delegated job. [Answer a question](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/#answer-a-question) shows it from your side. |
| `delegate_jobs`                   | Start independent jobs on other repositories or on the same one, and resume when they finish                                                      | When [orchestration](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/orchestration/index.md) is on, which is the default, and the run is not a delegated leg                                                                                                                                                       |

## Tools loaded on demand

The agent loads these tools through `tool_search`, a tool that finds a tool by what it does and loads its definition. This keeps the list of tools the model sees short. A tool the agent loads stays available for the rest of the session. Setting `DEFERRED_TOOLS_ENABLED` to `false` binds every tool up front instead; [Deferred tools](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#deferred-tools) describes it and its related settings.

| Tool                                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | When the agent has it                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gitlab`                                        | Inspect and update issues, merge requests, pipelines, job logs and releases                                                                                                                                                                                                | On a GitLab repository                                                                                                                                |
| `gh`                                            | The same, through the `gh` command line                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | On a GitHub repository                                                                                                                                |
| `web_search`                                    | Search the web through DuckDuckGo, Tavily or SearXNG                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | When web search is on, which is the default. [Web search](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#web-search) describes the settings. |
| `web_fetch`                                     | Fetch a URL, convert it to Markdown and answer a prompt about its content                                                                                                                                                                                                  | When web fetch is on, which is the default. [Web fetch](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#web-fetch) describes the settings.    |
| `publish_artifact`                              | Copy a workspace file, such as an HTML report, a CSV or a chart, into DAIV as an [artifact](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/#artifacts) and return its viewer URL. With `artifact_id`, it replaces the file of an artifact the session already published. | Always                                                                                                                                                |
| `fetch_artifact`                                | Copy an artifact the session already published back into `/workspace/tmp`, so the agent can revise it                                                                                                                                                                      | Always                                                                                                                                                |
| `check_delegated_jobs`, `cancel_delegated_jobs` | Check, or cancel, the jobs the agent delegated                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | When `delegate_jobs` is available                                                                                                                     |
| MCP tools                                       | The tools of the [MCP servers](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/mcp-tools/index.md) the run has, such as Sentry or Context7                                                                                                                                    | When an MCP server is enabled for the run                                                                                                             |

## Model priority

The agent runs on the first model that a source sets, from a model you pick for the run, through the `daiv-max` issue label and the repository's `.daiv.yml`, to the site's settings. [Model overrides](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/customization/repository-config/#model-overrides) lists the order. A subagent follows its own order, described in [Subagent model precedence](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/subagents/#subagent-model-precedence), and [Environment variables](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#daiv-agent) lists the settings.

# Monitoring

DAIV reports on its agent runs in two places. [LangSmith](https://smith.langchain.com) holds the trace of each run: latency, tool calls and intermediate steps. DAIV's own database holds each run's token usage and estimated cost, and a copy of each session's conversation. This page covers both, and the log events DAIV writes when something needs an operator.

## Trace runs with LangSmith

DAIV sends a trace of every agent run to LangSmith once you set three variables. You need a LangSmith account.

1. In [LangSmith](https://smith.langchain.com), select **Settings** → **API Keys** → **Create API Key**.

1. Copy the key.

1. Set `LANGSMITH_TRACING` to `true`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT` to the project to write traces to, and `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` to the key. [Monitoring (LangSmith)](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#monitoring-langsmith) describes each variable, including the Docker secret form of the key and the EU endpoint.

   ```
   x-app-defaults: &x_app_default
     environment:
       LANGSMITH_TRACING: true
       LANGSMITH_PROJECT: daiv-production
       LANGSMITH_API_KEY: <langsmith-api-key>
   ```

   Replace `<langsmith-api-key>` with your LangSmith API key.

1. Recreate the services so they read the variables. On Docker Compose, run:

   ```
   docker compose up -d
   ```

   On Docker Swarm, run:

   ```
   docker stack deploy -c stack.yml daiv
   ```

1. Start a run, for example a chat in the dashboard. A trace appears in your LangSmith project.

## Trace tags and metadata

Every agent run carries tags and metadata that you can filter and group by in LangSmith. The title and commit message generation run has its own, described below.

An agent run has these tags:

| Tag             | Description                    | Example                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| Git platform    | The platform of the repository | `gitlab`, `github`                 |
| Repository slug | The repository the run targets | `group/project`                    |
| Scope           | The conversation scope         | `Issue`, `Merge Request`, `Global` |
| Agent name      | The agent that ran             | `DAIV Agent`                       |

The scope tag is absent when the run has no scope. A run on a labelled GitLab issue carries `gitlab`, `group/project`, `Issue` and `DAIV Agent`.

Its metadata holds these fields:

| Field              | Type           | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `repository`       | string         | Repository slug, for example `group/project`                                                        |
| `git_platform`     | string         | `gitlab` or `github`                                                                                |
| `scope`            | string         | `Issue`, `Merge Request` or `Global`                                                                |
| `trigger`          | string         | What started the run: `label`, `mention`, `job`, `chat` or `diff_to_metadata`                       |
| `model`            | string         | Primary model of the run, as a full model spec such as `openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`     |
| `thinking_level`   | string         | Thinking level of the run; absent when the run has none                                             |
| `lc_agent_name`    | string         | The agent name, `DAIV Agent`                                                                        |
| `author`           | string         | User who created the issue or merge request (issue and merge request runs)                          |
| `triggered_by`     | string         | User who triggered the run, who differs from the author on a mention (issue and merge request runs) |
| `issue_id`         | int            | Issue IID (issue runs)                                                                              |
| `labels`           | list           | The issue's labels, lowercased (issue runs)                                                         |
| `merge_request_id` | int            | Merge request ID (merge request runs)                                                               |
| `ref`              | string         | The branch the run was asked to use (job runs)                                                      |
| `override_source`  | string or null | `explicit` when the request picked the model, otherwise `null` (job and chat runs)                  |

A run on a labelled issue has `trigger` set to `label`, and a run started by an `@daiv` mention on an issue, or on a merge request no session owns, has it set to `mention`. A chat message that starts a run on an idle session has `chat` and the `Global` scope. Every run DAIV takes from a session's inbox has `job` and the `Global` scope, as do runs from the [jobs API](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/jobs-api/index.md), a schedule or the MCP endpoint. The inbox holds pipeline watch fixes, chat messages queued while the session was busy, delegation resumes and leg follow-ups, and `@daiv` mentions on a merge request the session owns.

The pull request title and commit message generation runs as a separate run named and tagged `DiffToMetadata`, with `trigger` set to `diff_to_metadata`. It carries the git platform, repository and scope tags and no agent name tag. It nests under the agent trace when DAIV publishes at the end of a run, and stands alone when DAIV recovers a draft.

## Create the LangSmith dashboard

DAIV creates a LangSmith dashboard named **DAIV Monitoring** with 27 charts in 8 groups, built on the tags and metadata above. You need the LangSmith variables from [Trace runs with LangSmith](#trace-runs-with-langsmith) set in the container.

Warning

Recreating the dashboard with `--recreate` deletes the existing **DAIV Monitoring** dashboard, including any chart you added by hand. [`setup_langsmith_dashboard`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#setup_langsmith_dashboard) describes it.

1. Run the command, with your project name:

   ```
   docker compose exec app django-admin setup_langsmith_dashboard --project <project-name>
   ```

   Replace `<project-name>` with your LangSmith project.

1. In LangSmith, open the **DAIV Monitoring** dashboard of your project.

After you upgrade DAIV, run the command with `--recreate` to add the charts the upgrade brings.

| Group              | Charts                                                                                                      | What it tracks                      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| **Overview**       | Trace volume and error rate by scope, trigger breakdown                                                     | Activity and reliability            |
| **Latency**        | Median and P99 latency by scope, latency by repository                                                      | Response times                      |
| **Cost**           | Total cost by scope, prompt against completion cost, token usage by repository, P99 cost per run by trigger | Spend                               |
| **Platform**       | Volume and error rate by git platform, top repositories by volume                                           | Platform and repository breakdown   |
| **Tools**          | Subagent usage, tool call volume, tool error rate, MCP server tool usage                                    | What the agent calls                |
| **LLM**            | Call count, latency, prompt against completion tokens                                                       | Model calls                         |
| **Model**          | Trace volume, latency, cost and error rate by model                                                         | Per-model comparison                |
| **DiffToMetadata** | Volume, latency, error rate                                                                                 | Title and commit message generation |

To compare models, group a chart by the `model` metadata field. To see who starts the runs, group by `author` or `triggered_by`.

## Usage and cost

DAIV records the token usage and an estimated cost for every agent run in its own database, without a LangSmith account.

DAIV counts the tokens of every model call in the run, including fallback models, models that tools call, and subagents, and prices each call on its own. For a call through OpenRouter, the cost is the charge OpenRouter reports, which depends on the provider it routed the call to. For any other call, DAIV estimates it from the model's list price in [genai-prices](https://github.com/pydantic/genai-prices). DAIV then totals the tokens and cost per model, and stores the totals on the run.

A run records:

| Field            | Description                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input_tokens`   | Input tokens across all model calls                                                        |
| `output_tokens`  | Output tokens across all model calls                                                       |
| `total_tokens`   | Input plus output tokens                                                                   |
| `cost_usd`       | The run's cost in US dollars                                                               |
| `usage_by_model` | The same figures per model, with the cache and reasoning token counts the provider reports |

Two limits apply:

- For a call DAIV prices from list prices, the cost is empty when genai-prices does not list the model, and a run's cost is empty when any of its calls has no price. The tokens are still recorded, and DAIV logs a warning naming the model.
- A cost priced from list prices is an estimate. Your provider's bill can differ.

You see the figures in three places. A row in the sessions list shows the session's cost, the **Spend** section of a session's **Overview** shows what the session cost, and a run's downloaded Markdown result holds `total_tokens` and `cost_usd` in its front matter. [Sessions](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sessions/index.md) describes the pages.

## Export session archives

DAIV writes a copy of each session's conversation to its database when each run ends. This session archive is the saved copy, not a session's **Archived** state. The copy outlives the checkpointer's time to live and LangSmith's retention, and you can export it for offline analysis.

Warning

An export holds full conversations and run prompts. Store the output directory as you would the repositories' contents, and delete it when you finish.

1. Run [`export_session_archives`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/management-commands/#export_session_archives) with an output directory, and with `--since` and `--repo` to narrow the sessions. The command's page holds the commands that write the files inside the container, copy them to the host and remove them.
1. Open `<thread_id>.json` for each session.

Each file holds the session's repository, origin and title, and its contexts in order, where a `/clear` closes one context and starts the next and `closed_at` says when. Each context holds its messages in LangChain's `messages_to_dict` format. The file also holds each run's status, model, tokens and cost. The archive holds the session's messages, not each model request: system prompts, tool schemas, summaries and subagent internals stay in LangSmith. When a session fails to export, the command logs and names it, writes the rest, then exits with an error.

## Log events

DAIV writes these events to its logs. Alert on them or search for them to find a problem early.

### Archive events

The `daiv.sessions` logger reports archive trouble. Errors reach Sentry.

| Level   | Message                                                                     | Meaning                                                                                                          |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ERROR   | `executor: failed to archive thread_id=…`                                   | A run's end was not archived, and the traceback says why, a timeout included. The next run's archive catches up. |
| ERROR   | `Thread … holds N messages, fewer than its archived M; keeping the archive` | The live thread lost messages the archive holds. DAIV leaves the archive as it was.                              |
| ERROR   | `Failed to load archived context N of thread …; leaving it out`             | An archive row no longer decodes, and the transcript shows without it.                                           |
| WARNING | `No session … to archive its thread under`                                  | A thread has no session, so DAIV archives nothing.                                                               |
| INFO    | `Restored thread … from archived context N`                                 | An expired thread was seeded from its archive before a run.                                                      |

A context that exists but fails to restore fails the run with `ArchiveRestoreError` and is not logged as one of these events.

### Bash policy events

The `daiv.tools` logger writes a warning when the [sandbox](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/sandbox/index.md) `bash` tool blocks a command, or cannot parse one and so blocks it.

```
[bash] bash_policy_denied: command denied (id=<call_id>, reason=default_disallow, rule='git push', segment='git push origin main')
```

```
[bash] bash_policy_parse_failed: command could not be parsed (id=<call_id>, reason='Parse error: ...')
```

Each record carries these fields:

| Field             | Description                                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event`           | `bash_policy_denied` or `bash_policy_parse_failed`                                      |
| `reason_category` | `default_disallow`, `global_disallow` or `parse_failure`                                |
| `matched_rule`    | The rule that blocked the command, for example `git push`; on `bash_policy_denied` only |
| `denied_segment`  | The part of the command that was blocked; on `bash_policy_denied` only                  |
| `tool_call_id`    | The agent's tool call ID, which matches the tool call in the LangSmith trace            |

`default_disallow` is a built-in rule, and `global_disallow` is a rule you set in `DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_DISALLOW`. A spike in `bash_policy_denied` means the agent keeps attempting a blocked command.

## Troubleshooting

### No traces appear in LangSmith

Check that `LANGSMITH_TRACING` is `true` and that the API key is correct. Check that the containers can reach the LangSmith endpoint, and read the application logs for authentication errors.

### A trace is incomplete

Check that the project name is the same in every service. On Docker Swarm, check that the secret holding the API key is mounted.

# Management commands

DAIV ships twelve `django-admin` commands for setup and operator repairs. Run them inside the app container:

```
docker compose exec app django-admin <command>
```

Four of the twelve run on their own, so a manual run is the exception:

| Command                                             | Runs on its own                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`setup_default_site`](#setup_default_site)         | On every container start                                      |
| [`setup_checkpoint_saver`](#setup_checkpoint_saver) | On every container start                                      |
| [`sync_stuck_runs`](#sync_stuck_runs)               | Every 5 minutes                                               |
| [`setup_webhooks`](#setup_webhooks)                 | On the `CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON` schedule, on GitLab only |

The other eight run only when you run them.

## `archive_sessions`

Copies the live checkpoint of every session that has no archive into the session archive, so the transcript outlives the checkpointer TTL. Run it once after upgrading to the release that archives sessions, before those checkpoints expire; `UPGRADING.md` says so. Running it again retries the sessions that failed. It does not run on its own.

This command takes no options.

```
docker compose exec app django-admin archive_sessions
```

## `backfill_memory_entries`

Rebuilds a repository's memory entries by replaying its historical consolidated observations through the consolidation operations pass, oldest first. It makes LLM calls. Running it again replays only the observations that no entry covers. It ignores the memory enabled flags, because it is an operator repair action. It does not run on its own.

Warning

`--reset-document` clears the repository's stored memory document before replaying. DAIV keeps the old text only in a WARNING log line, so copy it from the command's output or your log pipeline if you may need it.

| Option             | Description                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--repo-id`        | Repository ID to backfill, for example `group/project`. Required.                                                    |
| `--batch-size`     | Observations per operations round, from 1 to 50. Default: `20`.                                                      |
| `--reset-document` | Clear the stored memory document before replaying. Use it for a repository whose document no replay can reconstruct. |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin backfill_memory_entries --repo-id group/project
```

## `bootstrap_admin`

Creates the initial admin user when no admin exists yet. The command refuses to run if an admin exists, or if a user with that email exists. The new admin signs in with a one-time code sent by email; see [Deployment](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/deployment/index.md). It does not run on its own.

| Argument | Description                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `email`  | Email address of the new admin user. |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin bootstrap_admin admin@example.com
```

## `consolidate_memory`

Consolidates the pending memory observations of one repository into its memory document, in the foreground. The shell waits for the consolidation model's LLM call, and the call is billed like any other. DAIV's own hourly sweep does not use this command; it enqueues consolidation for the repositories that are due. This command does not run on its own.

Without `--force`, the command refuses to run while fewer than 10 observations are pending.

| Option      | Description                                                          |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--repo-id` | Repository ID to consolidate, for example `group/project`. Required. |
| `--force`   | Consolidate even below the pending-observation threshold.            |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin consolidate_memory --repo-id group/project
```

## `create_api_key`

Creates an API key for a user, for the [Jobs API](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/jobs-api/index.md) and other API clients. The key is printed once, on creation. It does not run on its own.

A time in `--expires-at` without an offset is read in `Europe/Lisbon`, not in the zone of your server or shell; see [Time zone](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/env-variables/#time-zone). Give an explicit offset to avoid the ambiguity.

| Argument / option | Description                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `username`        | Username of the user to create the key for.                                                           |
| `--name`          | Name of the key. Default: empty.                                                                      |
| `--expires-at`    | Expiry in ISO 8601 format, for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59+00:00`. Default: the key does not expire. |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin create_api_key <username> --name "my-key" --expires-at 2026-12-31T23:59:59+00:00
```

Replace `<username>` with the username of the key's owner.

## `export_session_archives`

Writes each archived session's contexts and runs to `<output>/<thread_id>.json`, for offline analysis. See [Export session archives](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/monitoring/#export-session-archives) for what an export holds. It does not run on its own.

The exports hold full conversations and run prompts. Inside the app container, a relative `output` resolves in the container, so the files never reach the host on their own. Write them to a temporary directory, copy them out, and delete the directory in the container.

| Argument / option | Description                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `output`          | Directory to write the files to. DAIV creates it if missing.   |
| `--since`         | Only sessions active on or after this date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.   |
| `--repo`          | Only sessions on this repository, for example `group/project`. |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin export_session_archives /tmp/session-exports --since 2026-10-01 --repo group/project
docker compose cp app:/tmp/session-exports ./session-exports
docker compose exec app rm -rf /tmp/session-exports
```

## `release_orphan_queued_sessions`

Releases queued runs whose session has no active sibling (a ready or running run). It mitigates a rare race where the dispatcher missed a terminal transition, or a run was created queued and never picked up; a sessions log message points here when that happens. It does not run on its own.

This command takes no options.

```
docker compose exec app django-admin release_orphan_queued_sessions
```

## `setup_checkpoint_saver`

Initializes the LangGraph Redis checkpointer indices. It runs on every container start, so run it by hand only after you reset the checkpointer's Redis store while DAIV is running.

This command takes no options.

```
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_checkpoint_saver
```

## `setup_default_site`

Updates the default Django `Site` domain from `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`, so sign-in emails link to the right host. It runs on every container start; run it by hand after you change `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL` without restarting.

This command takes no options.

```
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_default_site
```

## `setup_langsmith_dashboard`

Creates the LangSmith custom dashboard **DAIV Monitoring**, with the monitoring charts for DAIV. See [Create the LangSmith dashboard](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/reference/monitoring/#create-the-langsmith-dashboard). It needs `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` set in the container. It does not run on its own.

Warning

`--recreate` deletes the existing **DAIV Monitoring** dashboard, including any chart you added to it by hand, and creates it again.

| Option       | Description                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--project`  | LangSmith project name. Default: the `LANGCHAIN_PROJECT` environment variable, then `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`, then `default`. |
| `--recreate` | Delete the existing dashboard and create it again. Without it, the command fails when the dashboard exists.              |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_langsmith_dashboard --project <project-name>
```

Replace `<project-name>` with your LangSmith project.

## `setup_webhooks`

Sets the DAIV webhook on every repository DAIV can access, so issue and merge request events reach the instance.

This command is GitLab only. GitHub webhooks are set in the GitHub App's configuration, so on GitHub the command logs a warning and returns; see [Platform setup](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/getting-started/platform-setup/index.md). On GitLab it also runs on its own on the `CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON` schedule, so run it by hand only to add webhooks right away, or with `--update` to change the existing ones.

Warning

`--disable-ssl-verification` makes GitLab post webhook payloads, with the secret token in the `X-Gitlab-Token` header, without checking DAIV's certificate. Use it for local setups with self-signed certificates only. The scheduled run sets it only when `DEBUG` is on.

Warning

A token passed with `--secret-token` lands in your shell history and shows in the process list while the command runs. Set `CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` instead, and keep the flag for one-off overrides.

| Option                       | Description                                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--base-url`                 | Base URL of DAIV. Default: `DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL`.                                  |
| `--repo-id`                  | Only set up this repository ID.                                                  |
| `--secret-token`             | Secret token for webhook validation. Overrides `CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |
| `--disable-ssl-verification` | Tell GitLab not to verify DAIV's SSL certificate for the webhook.                |
| `--update`                   | Update existing webhooks as well as creating missing ones.                       |

```
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_webhooks --update
```

## `sync_stuck_runs`

Reconciles runs that are not in a terminal state:

- Task-backed runs are re-synced from their linked task result.
- Inline chat runs that a worker crash left running are failed once their session heartbeat goes stale. Task-backed job and inbox runs in the same state are failed the same way.
- Ready runs whose submitter stopped before queueing their task are failed once they are old enough.

It runs on its own every 5 minutes, so run it by hand only to reconcile right away.

This command takes no options.

```
docker compose exec app django-admin sync_stuck_runs
```

# Benchmarks

DAIV's [`/code-review`](https://docs.daivagent.com/dev/features/slash-commands/#code-review) is measured on [ReviewBench](https://github.com/review-bench/ReviewBench), an open benchmark of real pull requests. Each pull request comes with a human-reviewed golden set of known issues. This page reports a baseline measured on 2026-10-27 at commit `d3f513a56`, how it was measured, and what it does not tell you.

______________________________________________________________________

## Code review on ReviewBench

|           |                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Benchmark | The ReviewBench test set: 25 pull requests from 25 repositories, 352 known issues                                                                                                          |
| Reviewer  | The `/code-review` skill as merged in [#1711](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/pull/1711), run at `d3f513a56`, on Claude Haiku 5.5 (`anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5`) with thinking level `xhigh` |
| Judge     | Claude Sonnet 5.5, as ReviewBench's matcher and classifier                                                                                                                                 |
| Runs      | One pass over all 25 pull requests, on 2026-10-27                                                                                                                                          |

### Results

Precision and recall are macro averages: every pull request weighs the same.

| Metric              | Result     |
| ------------------- | ---------- |
| Grounded precision  | 92.1%      |
| Grounded recall     | 44.6%      |
| Augmented precision | 88.9%      |
| Augmented recall    | 58.6%      |
| Known issues found  | 150 of 352 |

The review reported 301 findings. 125 matched a known issue, 136 matched none but the judge classified them as valid (novel true positives), and 40 were false positives. One finding can match more than one known issue, so known issues found (150) is higher than matched findings (125).

### Recall by category and severity

Known issues found out of all known issues in that category or severity, pooled over the 25 pull requests rather than averaged per pull request.

| Category         | Known issues | Found | Recall |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ----- | ------ |
| Correctness      | 133          | 63    | 47.4%  |
| Reliability      | 58           | 32    | 55.2%  |
| Maintainability  | 44           | 7     | 15.9%  |
| Testing          | 35           | 13    | 37.1%  |
| Security         | 27           | 15    | 55.6%  |
| Documentation    | 21           | 5     | 23.8%  |
| API architecture | 12           | 4     | 33.3%  |
| Performance      | 12           | 9     | 75.0%  |
| Accessibility    | 10           | 2     | 20.0%  |

| Severity | Known issues | Found | Recall |
| -------- | ------------ | ----- | ------ |
| High     | 36           | 21    | 58.3%  |
| Medium   | 134          | 79    | 59.0%  |
| Low      | 182          | 50    | 27.5%  |

The weak spots are low-severity issues, maintainability and documentation.

### Cost and time

|                      |                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Cost, all 25 reviews | $7.75, about $0.31 per review        |
| Cost per review      | From $0.05 to $1.47                  |
| Time per review      | 8.3 minutes on average, 20.3 at most |

Cost is the model usage of the review agent and its detectors, priced by DAIV's usage tracking at Anthropic's list prices. It does not include the judge or the sandbox.

______________________________________________________________________

## How it was measured

**Review.** [`evals/reviewbench.py`](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/evals/reviewbench.py) fetches each pull request's base and head from its ReviewBench mirror and runs `/code-review` on the head in a DAIV sandbox. The network is off and the reviewer has no MCP servers and no web tools, because the upstream pull request's review comments are a source of the golden set. The driver writes the findings in ReviewBench's judging format.

**Judging.** ReviewBench's judge compares the findings with the golden set. A matcher model pairs each finding with the known issues it describes. A classifier model labels each finding the matcher left unmatched as valid or a false positive. Both ran on Claude Sonnet 5.5.

**Grounded and augmented.** Grounded metrics count only the golden set. Grounded precision looks only at findings matched to a golden-set entry: the share whose entry is a known issue rather than one the golden set labels a false positive. Grounded recall is the share of known issues found. Augmented metrics also count the classifier's verdicts on unmatched findings. Augmented precision is the share of all findings that are valid, and augmented recall adds the novel true positives to both the found and the total. ReviewBench's [methodology](https://github.com/review-bench/ReviewBench/blob/main/docs/METHODOLOGY.md) defines all four.

______________________________________________________________________

## Limits

- **25 pull requests.** The test set is a sample of the 219-pull-request full set, which DAIV has not been measured on.
- **One pass.** Results move between identical runs. Two identical runs on the 14 smaller pull requests found 70 and 67 known issues, with single pull requests moving by up to 3.
- **An LLM judge.** The judge model changes the scores. On the same findings, Sonnet 5.5 counted 32 false positives where Sonnet 5 counted 17.
- **Augmented recall grows with the reviewer's own findings.** Its denominator includes the reviewer's novel true positives, so ReviewBench recommends grounded recall for comparing reviewers.
- **One reviewer configuration.** Only Claude Haiku 5.5 at `xhigh` was measured on this version of the skill. Other models will score differently.
- **One retried pull request.** jadx took three attempts: the driver rejected the first report because it lacked the `## Code Review` heading, and the second review skipped the skill. The third is the one scored. The first two cost $0.13, which is not in the cost above.

Not a leaderboard result

This is an offline run. The [ReviewBench leaderboard](https://review-bench.ai) scores all 219 pull requests three times through its own portal, judged by Claude Sonnet 5. These numbers are not a leaderboard submission and are not comparable with leaderboard entries.

______________________________________________________________________

## Experiment log and reproducing

The [experiment log](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/evals/results/reviewbench/README.md#experiment-log) lists each measured change to the code-review skill with its result and verdict, the changes that were dropped included. The [baseline files](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/tree/main/evals/results/reviewbench/baseline) hold the findings, the judge's scores per finding and the usage per agent.

To reproduce the run, follow [How to run](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/evals/results/reviewbench/README.md#how-to-run): start a local DAIV stack, run `evals/reviewbench.py` on the 25 pull requests, then score the findings with ReviewBench's `npm run judge` on Claude Sonnet 5.5.
# Community

# Community

DAIV is open-source and contributions are welcome — code, documentation, testing, or feedback.

## Contributing

For contribution guidelines, code style, testing requirements, and the pull request process, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Questions and ideas

Ask for setup help and share ideas in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/discussions).

## Reporting issues

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/issues) for bug reports and feature requests. Search existing issues first; the issue forms ask for the version, platform and logs a report needs.

Report security vulnerabilities privately, as described in the [security policy](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/SECURITY.md), never in a public issue.

## Code of conduct

Everyone taking part in the project is expected to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## License and funding

DAIV is [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/LICENSE) licensed, and it has no paid tier. It is maintained by Sandro Rodrigues.

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/srtab/daiv/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
